# CUDA efficient-attention screen

Prospective declaration, 2026-10-05. The engine task owns this bounded screen.
The preceding FP32 batch-one and batch-eight controls passed all 77 strict
CPU-reference gates; the released BF16 recipe failed. No production dtype or
attention policy changes here.

## Hypothesis and arithmetic boundary

An explicit full causal mask may let the maintained Transformers SDPA path
expand eight KV heads to sixteen query heads and use PyTorch efficient
attention on FP32 tensors. This could avoid the unfused math attention path,
but expansion and mask construction add work. CUDA attention's ordinary time
fraction has not been measured, so no Amdahl gain or whole-engine ceiling is
predicted from the Mac profiles.

The actual frozen Transformers `5.18.0` integration repeats KV heads when a
mask is present on this Linux/CUDA path. Prepared 4D masks are accepted by its
masking integration. The candidate supplies a fresh `[1,1,L,L]` Boolean mask,
with `True` exactly when key position is no later than query position. It uses
full prefill, no past state and `use_cache=False`. Right padding follows all
observed query/candidate endpoints; masking future positions preserves their
causal domain. Scalar `L=1` remains a full one-token causal domain.

Force `SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` inside the adapter's forward. The inner
context must override the unchanged FP32 scorer's outer math-only context;
unsupported execution must fail visibly rather than silently fall back to math.
Mask construction and maintained KV expansion belong inside inference. There
is no retained mask cache or duplicated model storage. The original scorer's
encoder, head, device and backbone ownership remain unchanged; a typed view
adapts only the backbone call at the frozen nominal type boundary.

FP32 input/output tensors and IEEE process matmul settings do **not** prove
IEEE arithmetic inside this candidate. PyTorch's version-tagged
[GEMM specialization](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/v2.12.1/aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/cuda/mem_eff_attention/gemm_kernel_utils.h)
selects CUTLASS `OpMultiplyAddFastF32` for float on SM80 and later; its
[forward kernel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/v2.12.1/aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/cuda/mem_eff_attention/kernel_forward.h)
uses that type for QK and probability-value products. This is a FastF32 quality
hypothesis, not exact arithmetic. The tag alone does not prove the installed
binary's internal implementation. Record its exact build and actual operator/
kernel observations; retain unobserved details as unknown.

PyTorch's maintained mask preprocessing may pad additive bias row strides for
efficient-kernel alignment. Record actual shapes, strides, mask dtype and
selector evidence rather than inventing a sequence-length restriction. The
[maintained attention implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/v2.12.1/aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/attention.cpp)
and observed dispatch are separate evidence.

## Frozen inputs and staged evidence

Preserve the six original CUDA source/test files, all twenty production files,
the v2 transfer manifest `f7d9d7a4…`, and the reviewed FP32 batch-one receipt
`d528a44e…` plus terminal wall receipt `cb00f5f0…` byte-for-byte. Admit all 44
canonical assets and exact package/build identities before GPU allocation.
Validate every original token, endpoint and query position against the pinned
CPU reference. Freeze the new source/test/declaration bytes separately and
check them before and after execution.

Use only the first eight cases in the original ordered 77-row BANKING77
training-source development cohort. In separate batch-one and batch-eight
jobs, run one ordinary math control cohort and one ordinary candidate cohort.
Retain all sixteen case outcomes per job, including errors and unknown cases.
Compare both arms with the original CPU reference and the admitted CUDA FP32
control: identical choices and full rankings, no accuracy decrease or failures,
logit absolute/relative tolerance `1e-3`, probability tolerance `1e-4`.

Only after ordinary quality passes, profile one control and one candidate
batch: the first case at batch one and all eight cases at batch eight. Retain
their outputs under the same gates. Record actual SDPA Q/K/V shapes, strides,
dtypes, mask and public selector diagnostics without retaining tensor owners.
Require an efficient-attention operator for every candidate layer and preserve
actual kernel names when available. Selector support is not observed execution;
an efficient operator is not proof of the precise arithmetic used internally.
Profile overhead and diagnostic events support no latency or throughput claim.
Failure of an ordinary arm stops before profiling, with attempted failures and
unstarted case IDs retained. No failed or unsupported sample is omitted.

Each job uses one owned fresh worker with a 180-second whole-process cap.
Require uncontended pre-allocation and per-batch observations; stop on foreign
compute ownership and never signal another job. Restore precision/backend
contexts and dispose observers before successful completion. Preserve partial
receipts, timeouts, source drift, write failures and cleanup failures.

Full77 confirmation, warmed alternating performance comparisons and production
selection need separate release after independent review of this screen. Eight
unique development cases cannot gate full77 behavior or held-out Wyat quality.
No timing or production result is accepted by this diagnostic screen.

## Prospective observer correction, 2026-10-05

The first batch-one receipt retains `dispatch_passed=false` and parent exit 1.
Its independent audit confirms all eighteen ordinary/profile outcomes passed
unchanged numerical and ranking gates. The public dispatcher observed twenty-eight
`aten.scaled_dot_product_attention.default` calls with FP32 equal-head Q/K/V
and the Boolean `[1,1,L,L]` causal mask. It does not expose internal C++ dispatch
or the converted additive bias. The profiler separately recorded twenty-eight
private efficient-attention operators, twenty-eight efficient forward operators,
and twenty-eight CUTLASS FP32 attention kernels. Original source text is retained
in the immutable first-run source archive; its declaration and flags remain
unchanged. This is an observation-boundary correction, not a quality-gate change.

For the second, separately hashed seven-file source declaration, require both:

- Exactly twenty-eight public SDPA observations with expected FP32 CUDA Q/K/V
  shapes and innermost strides, plus the fresh Boolean causal-mask shape.
  Require effective dropout zero, causal flag false, GQA flag false and default
  scale: either omitted (`None`) or a finite float exactly `128**-0.5`. The
  frozen HF/Qwen source explicitly supplies that numeric mathematical default.
  Resolve positional/keyword arguments and pinned schema defaults, preserving
  the observed representation rather than requiring omission.
  Label these metadata as preceding PyTorch's bias conversion and padding.
  Causal mask contents are supported by construction and exact mask tests;
  metadata alone observes only shape, dtype and strides.
- Exactly twenty-eight private efficient-attention and forward profiler events,
  no math/Flash/cuDNN fallback events, and twenty-eight actual FP32 CUTLASS
  attention kernel events in the pinned runtime.

Record public selector diagnostics using those same effective call arguments
at their actual boundary. `SDPAParams` cannot encode an explicit scale; label
that API limit even when the observed value is the mathematical default.
Eligibility before
bias preprocessing is diagnostic only; it cannot establish execution or reject
an internally prepared mask that the recorded kernel accepted. Converted bias
strides remain unknown. Kernel names support executed implementation identity,
not proof of IEEE internal arithmetic. Preserve missing kernel observations and
all failures; do not infer a pass from public metadata or forced context alone.

First rerun the eight-case batch-one screen with this corrected observer and
new source identity. Only its independently reviewed success releases the same
eight-case batch-eight screen. Both keep the original numerical/ranking gates,
ordinary/profile outcome counts, occupancy checks and 180-second parent caps.
No original receipt is overwritten. These repeated observations add no unique
quality cases and support no latency, full77 or production claim.

# Maintained BF16 MLP products: prospective protocol

This is a new experiment after [the exact FP16 storage family](precision.md)
failed its parameter eligibility guard. It retains the checkpoint's native
BF16 weights exactly and deliberately approximates selected projection inputs
and product outputs. No production precision policy changes.

Exactly three arms are fixed, in order: all 28 down projections, all 28 gate/up
projections, and all 28 complete MLPs. No layer narrowing or added arm follows a
failure. Each selected bias-free Linear must survive finite exact
FP32 → BF16 → FP32 weight equality before scoring. Nonselected weights and the
eager full-prefill FP32 control remain unchanged.

Gate/up arms share one BF16 input cast, use maintained BF16 Linear products,
and restore each output to FP32 before maintained SwiGLU. Down arms cast the
FP32 SwiGLU result to BF16, use maintained BF16 Linear, and restore its output
to FP32 before residual addition. Embeddings, attention, norms, residuals and
head remain FP32. Maintained accumulation does not undo activation or final
product rounding. Source/product dtype checks reject unintended promotion.

Fresh candidate module owners share immutable unmodified control arrays. Only
one candidate arm is resident alongside the FP32 control; references are deleted,
GC runs, the device synchronizes and inactive buffers are cleared between arms.
No prefix state is constructed or reused. Exact weight checks and synchronized
preparation time/memory are outside timed comparisons and retained separately.
The process owns a temporary 512 MiB inactive-cache cap, restored on all exits,
and both scorers use token cache zero. The fresh child starts with
`MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0` before importing MLX; whole-model compilation is disabled.

Every arm screens all 77 frozen training-source cases at batch eight and scalar,
with original candidate order, segmented rendering and the unchanged CPU FP32
reference. The initial FP32 control must itself pass both shapes. Existing gates
remain logit atol/rtol 0.001, probability atol 0.0001, identical top choices and
full ranks, finite values, complete coverage and no labeled-accuracy loss. All
three arms' raw failures and successes are retained before timing any survivor.
These cases are development evidence; prior released-model exposure is unknown.

The screen parent bounds its owned child to 180 seconds. Per-shape partial
receipts retain rows. `completed=true, passed=false` is a completed numerical
negative, distinct from an incomplete exception or timeout. Screen `passed`
means at least one of the three arms passed both shapes; individual outcomes
remain explicit. Existing receipts are never overwritten. Source/model/data/
reference identities are frozen before model loading.

Only dual-shape numerical survivors may receive timing, in the declared arm
order. Each survivor has a separate 180-second parent, checks the prior full
family's identities/rows/quality history, then independently rescreens itself
and the control on both shapes. It performs five alternating warmed whole-cohort
pairs at batch eight, then scalar. All warm and measured cycles must pass the
CPU reference gates; raw predictions, telemetry and flushed cycle journals are
retained. Acceptance requires median paired speedup ≥1.02 and paired sample p05
>1 at both shapes. No candidate is chosen by its fastest pair; all admitted
survivors are confirmed. Repeating the same cohort is performance confirmation,
not independent quality validation. A timeout, late restoration/write error or
failed numerical cycle cannot become a passing confirmation.

Prepared screen command; the coordinator must release the shared compute window
after independent source/tiny review before execution:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m benchmarks.analysis.mlx.bfloat.run \
  --output benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-bfloat-mlp-screen77.json
```

For a survivor, the fixed confirmation uses `--time-arm all-down` (or its
declared surviving name), `--screen` pointing to that completed family receipt,
and a fresh `--output` name. Source, test and declaration bytes stay fixed through
all confirmations. No real screen or timing has run at declaration time.
Production consideration also requires unchanged numerical behavior on the
frozen longer, variable-menu admitted native DMBench cases, plus independent
review; this short six-choice cohort alone cannot promote a precision policy.

## Observed result: all three arms rejected

The real screen completed within its bound: parent elapsed 28.515 seconds,
exit 1, no timeout or unexpected error. The exact BF16 parameter guards passed,
but every arm failed the unchanged numerical gates at both shapes. The FP32
control passed all 154 outputs, with maximum logit difference `1.502e-5` and
probability difference `3.070e-6` against the frozen CPU reference.

| Arm | Batch | Max logit difference | Max probability difference | Equal full ranks |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All down | 8 | 0.010673 | 0.002195 | 76 / 77 |
| All down | 1 | 0.016596 | 0.003832 | 77 / 77 |
| All gate/up | 8 | 0.018668 | 0.002426 | 74 / 77 |
| All gate/up | 1 | 0.032235 | 0.005736 | 77 / 77 |
| All MLP | 8 | 0.030442 | 0.006597 | 74 / 77 |
| All MLP | 1 | 0.019596 | 0.003965 | 71 / 77 |

All 462 candidate predictions were finite, with matching top choices and 67/77
correct per cycle. Those observations do not compensate for failed logit,
probability and full-ranking constraints. No numerical survivor entered timing,
no five-pair confirmation ran, and no production precision policy changed.
Retained screen latencies are numerical diagnostics, not a supported speed gain.
Parameter checks and candidate preparation took approximately 165.48, 229.00
and 263.43 ms respectively, outside scoring and timing comparisons.

The [raw receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-bfloat-mlp-screen77.json)
retains the FP32 controls and every declared arm/shape output. Its SHA256 is
`f554d04edfd73a69c4e5fdf417a8dacd752b90a49480eba1f0ce4443029f3504`.
The [parent receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-bfloat-mlp-screen77.wall.json)
distinguishes a completed numerical negative from timeout or incomplete failure.
The prospective declaration, reviewed source and tests remain in
[the immutable executed archive](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-bfloat-mlp-screen77.sources-75a93ba0c33c30b6.json),
whose full SHA256 is
`75a93ba0c33c30b6cd23a0c2bbf363d56581e7922c4d7768671d26e81d3d1d99`.

Before execution, 14 pure protocol checks and 13 tiny CPU recipe/ownership/
property checks passed independently, including PyTorch Linear/SwiGLU oracles,
variable candidate counts/lengths, scalar/batch readouts and malformed prior
screen history. Independent final audit reconstructed all 616 raw control and
candidate outcomes and their per-shape CPU gates, verified frozen source and
pinned identities, and confirmed the non-passing parent status. These results
are limited to this pinned checkpoint and development cohort, with no held-out
quality or performance claim. Parent and child processes exited and the coordinated
CPU/RAM/Metal window was released before any subsequent work.

# Measure inactive cache separately from active model memory

The experiment in `benchmarks.analysis.mlx.cache` tests whether bounding MLX's
inactive allocator cache reduces retained memory without changing real model
outputs. It compares the fresh process's original cache cap with 512 MiB and
1 GiB at one fixed engine batch size. It does not change production settings.

MLX's cache retains reusable inactive buffers. It is separate from prompt KV
state and Wyat's token-encoding cache. Active allocations hold the live model
and work; inactive buffers can remain allocated after that work completes.
`get_peak_memory()` reports peak active allocation, so active plus cache is
recorded separately. The cap is a reuse guideline: a freed buffer can cause a
small transient overshoot rather than a strict process-memory ceiling.
The [pinned allocator source](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.3/mlx/backend/metal/allocator.cpp)
and [cache-limit API](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/python/_autosummary/mlx.core.set_cache_limit.html)
define these mechanics. The setter returns the previous cap; the installed
API has no corresponding getter.

The real workload remains all 77 pinned BANKING77 training-source development
cases, the same six choices in original order, the same FP32 model and the
same token IDs/endpoints checked against the frozen CPU reference. Cache zero
for token encoding, eager execution and GPU device remain fixed. Released
model exposure to these queries is unknown; this is no held-out quality score.

Each cap receives five paired comparisons against the original setting.
Pair order alternates; the second cap begins in reverse order so original
and capped arms occupy the first position five times each across ten pairs.
Before **every** measured sample, both arms receive the same treatment:

1. Synchronize, set the declared cap, clear inactive cache, reset active peak.
2. Run one full-cohort warmup and retain its outputs, timing and memory.
3. Reset active peak, record synchronized memory, process counters and swap.
4. Time one complete cohort with native host-float output synchronization.
5. Record memory, process counters and swap outside the timed call.

Loading, clearing, warmups, telemetry and JSON persistence are excluded from
measured cohort time. This controlled warm-per-sample design bounds cache
history; it does not represent uninterrupted serving with variable shapes.
It also cannot attribute the earlier scaling delays to inactive buffers.

Every warmup and measured cycle must preserve all selections and full ranks,
logits within absolute/relative tolerance `1e-3`, probabilities within `1e-4`,
no failures and no labeled accuracy decline. Raw outputs and diagnostics are
flushed to JSONL after every sample. Failed gates produce a nonzero CLI exit.
The original cap is restored in `finally`, including model-load/sample errors.
Failed calls are excluded from successful requests/s. Failed-quality arms
retain timings for diagnosis and cannot support equivalent-throughput claims.

The receipt records synchronized active, inactive cache, their sum, and active
peak. It also retains cumulative process faults, CPU times, context switches,
load averages and wall timestamps around warmups and measurements. These
counter brackets include untimed synchronization/snapshot collection and are
not pure GPU counters. `sysctl vm.swapusage` is a global untimed observation;
changes do not establish which process caused them. Exact source bytes are
archived before loading; setup-time disk bytes do not attest already-imported
code or external dependency execution.

```sh
python -m benchmarks.analysis.mlx.cache .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B
```

Fake-only regression tests check paired ordering, restoration on both model
load and sample failures, and CLI rejection of failed quality. They replace
allocator/model calls; importing the installed MLX module still requires a
Metal-enabled session.

## Observed resource tradeoff

The [batch-8 receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-cache77-b8.json)
and [singleton receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-cache77-b1.json)
both completed. Across the two studies, every one of 80 warmup/measured
cohorts preserved all selections and full rankings; each cohort classified
67/77 labels correctly. The largest logit/probability differences against
CPU FP32 were `1.5021e-5` / `3.0703e-6`. Both processes restored the measured
original cache cap of 24481313587 bytes before exiting.

| Engine batch | Inactive cache cap | End-of-cohort active + cache GB | Overall requests/s, original → capped | Median paired speedup | Paired p05–p95 |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | 512 MiB | 9.317 → 2.926 | 27.53 → 27.33 | 0.9932 | 0.9907–0.9943 |
| 8 | 1 GiB | 9.317 → 3.464 | 27.51 → 27.20 | 0.9903 | 0.9841–0.9910 |
| 1 | 512 MiB | 6.817 → 2.926 | 23.24 → 22.79 | 0.9804 | 0.9784–0.9831 |
| 1 | 1 GiB | 6.817 → 3.464 | 23.19 → 22.97 | 0.9902 | 0.9896–0.9922 |

GB uses decimal bytes; configured MiB/GiB use powers of 1024. Active allocation
remained 2.388 GB in all end-of-cohort snapshots. Peak active was 3.847 GB at
batch 8 and 3.018 GB at batch 1, essentially unchanged by the cap. Inactive
cache accounted for the observed allocation reduction: default end-of-cohort
cache was 6.928 GB and 4.429 GB respectively. The bounded cache sometimes
exceeded its nominal cap slightly, consistent with allocator source mechanics.
These snapshots describe MLX allocation accounting, not process RSS or physical
page residency.

512 MiB reduced end-of-cohort active-plus-cache bytes by 68.6% at batch 8 and
57.1% at batch 1, with approximately 0.7% and 1.9% lower overall throughput.
The observed benefit is a memory tradeoff, not faster inference. Five pairs
are insufficient to estimate rare-tail stability. No large stalls occurred
in these controlled-reset samples and every measured process major-fault
delta was zero; neither observation establishes the cause of historical
outliers or guarantees behavior under uninterrupted serving.

For singleton reproduction, use a separate output:

```sh
python -m benchmarks.analysis.mlx.cache .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --batch-size 1 --output benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-cache77-b1.json
```

The separate `benchmarks.analysis.mlx.confirm_batches` experiment uses a fresh
process with unchanged default allocator behavior, one initial warm per shape,
and five alternating batch-2/batch-8 pairs. It never changes the cache cap or
clears between arms. This avoids treating the cache study's per-sample reset
design as evidence for ordinary continuous batching. Its two-shape history
still cannot reproduce the earlier six-shape workload exactly.

The [fresh continuous-default confirmation](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-batch2-8-confirm77.json)
preserved every output/ranking in both warmups and all ten measured cohorts,
with 67/77 labeled answers correct each time. Batch 8's median paired speedup
over batch 2 was 1.165×, paired p05–p95 1.008–1.355×; one of five pairs was
slower at 0.991×. Overall requests/s was 22.65 versus 26.29. Those five pairs
support batch 8 throughput for this ready cohort while retaining substantial
variation, not an online serving latency recommendation.

Both shapes finished with 14.276 GB inactive cache plus 2.388 GB active,
16.664 GB total allocator accounting. This differs from cleared/warmed batch
8's 6.928 GB inactive cache: loading and continuous variable-shape execution
history matter to allocator retention. Two measured cycles had process
major-fault deltas of one; other measured cycles had zero. They do not
establish a cause for delay. These observations make a controlled bounded
cache experiment with continuous variable-shape history a useful next
hypothesis, without revising the original six-shape evidence.

```sh
python -m benchmarks.analysis.mlx.confirm_batches .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B
```

# FP32 CPU experiment

Investigation and completed thread sweep on 2026-10-05. Eight configured
intra-op threads gave the highest observed throughput among the six sampled
counts. All 42 warmup/measured cohorts passed the frozen FP32 quality gates.
No production setting changed. A subsequent bounded operator profile confirmed
that this build already dispatches grouped-query attention to CPU flash.

The current Torch Kai path loads local Safetensors into FP32 `Qwen3Model`, uses
`eval()`/`inference_mode()`, disables KV caching, performs one causal SDPA
prefill and applies the FP32 candidate head after gathering endpoints. It pads
to each batch's exact longest sequence, without a redundant padding mask.
There is no vocabulary projection or generation loop to eliminate. See
[the scorer](../../wyat/backends/kai/torch.py) and
[completed CPU experiments](../torch-inference.md).

## Observed build and prior measurements

A read-only `torch.__config__.show()`/`parallel_info()` check found Torch 2.14.1
at build commit `5c4886908584029761b579af026dcfb627c84070`, Apple Accelerate
BLAS/LAPACK, OpenMP enabled, MKL disabled and MKLDNN disabled.
`torch.backends.mkldnn.is_available()` returned false even though its enabled
flag was true. Defaults were eight intra-operation threads and twelve
inter-operation threads. Enabling oneDNN flags cannot add absent compiled
kernels. The build-reported twelve hardware threads do not establish a uniform
core topology; a sandboxed `sysctl` topology query was unavailable.

The earlier [16-case screen](../../benchmarks/real/torch-causal-screen.json)
recorded these full-cohort causal-engine median times, over three repetitions:

| Intra-op count | Batch 1 | Batch 4 | Batch 8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2388.6 ms | 2010.0 ms | 2003.3 ms |
| 4 | 1980.6 ms | 1473.0 ms | 1385.5 ms |
| 8 | 1987.1 ms | 1343.1 ms | 1267.8 ms |

This screen suggests an effect on substantial backbone work: batch-eight
throughput at eight threads was about `1.58×` one thread, but only `1.09×` four
threads. Counts were screened in blocks rather than balanced thread comparisons;
these ratios are exploratory, not confirmed effects. This earlier screen did
not establish an optimum above eight threads. All screen ranks/selections
matched the explicit-mask path. The full 77-case reference remains the numerical
authority for the completed experiment.

CPU Inductor was already slower in all five warm pairs (`0.919×` median), and
QNNPACK INT8 was slower and failed numerical/rank gates. Mask removal gave a
simpler causal path without a meaningful CPU speedup. Repeating these unchanged
candidates would provide less information than the thread experiment.

## Completed six-count receipt

The [full receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-threads77.json)
retains every output and before/after diagnostic. It uses batch eight, all 77
canonical development cases, FP32/SDPA, no cache, one warmup and six balanced
measured cycles per count. Inter-op count remained twelve. Python was 3.12.11,
Torch 2.14.1 and Transformers 5.18.0. Throughput divides all 462 measured
requests at a count by their total synchronous cohort time; it is not a
singleton response-latency estimate.

| Configured intra-op count | Equivalent requests/s | Median cohort time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 8.364 | 9.209 s |
| 2 | 10.304 | 7.461 s |
| 4 | 11.957 | 6.440 s |
| 6 | 13.035 | 5.897 s |
| 8 | 13.396 | 5.718 s |
| 12 | 13.102 | 5.874 s |

All 36 measured and six warmup cohorts passed: 3,234 outputs retained, no
failed cases, identical selections and complete rankings. Across them, maximum
absolute logit drift was `8.345e-6` and probability drift `1.786e-6` against
the frozen CPU reference. Accuracy remained 67/77 in every cohort; this assay
does not establish held-out model quality. Eight threads achieved `1.602×`
the one-thread measured throughput. Twelve did not improve on eight. Same-round
ratios support this sampled comparison, not an independently confirmed global
optimum.

The [parent wall receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-threads77.wall.json)
reports 287.548 seconds within the 600-second cap, exit zero and no timeout.
The [setup source archive](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-threads77.sources-ee621c18dc3d4e8a.json)
contains eleven declared source files; its digest
`ee621c18dc3d4e8a99c8e7e8837676f5b8e1d32bf2964231d85cc23fade0e10f`
and each stored source hash were independently rechecked. This archives source
at setup, not dependencies or large checkpoints.

The first, excluded one-thread warmup recorded 139 major and 21,167 minor
faults. Every measured cycle had zero major faults; fault counts therefore do
not establish a paging explanation for measured outliers. OS one-minute load
ranged 1.58–3.43 across all snapshots. Own-process context switches and CPU
times are retained, with snapshot collection taking 2.6–17.5 microseconds
outside inference timing. These counters do not reveal exact Accelerate
worker topology, competing jobs, thermal state or DRAM traffic.

The descriptive USL fit gives `alpha=0.54594`, `beta=0.0047148`, throughput
`R²=0.9757`, maximum relative residual 4.38%, and a predicted peak near
9.814 configured threads. There are no confidence intervals or identified
physical mechanism. The fitted parameters do not establish serialization or
cache-coherence causes on this heterogeneous machine.

## Is nine or ten threads worth checking?

The same fitted curve predicts only `1.00251×` at nine and `1.00303×` at ten
versus **fitted** eight-thread throughput. Its ten-thread prediction is 13.197
requests/s, 1.48% below **observed** eight-thread throughput. That 0.30% fitted
increment is smaller than both the 4.38% fit residual and the eight-thread
cycle range of 5.687–5.869 seconds (3.22%). Interpolation is a hypothesis,
not evidence that ten improves performance. Testing both nine and ten adds
little information at this stage.

If a resource window is released, a narrow eight-versus-ten check can falsify
the peak suggestion: unchanged full cohort and batch eight, cache off, one
warmup per count, five adjacent pairs with alternating arm order, all raw
outputs/diagnostics retained and the existing strict quality gates. Freeze the
sources/reference before loading, hold inter-op twelve, restore prior intra-op
state, and retain a 600-second parent cap. Five pairs can detect a substantial
effect; they are not assumed to resolve a 0.30% difference. Do not change the
eight-thread reference on a fitted peak or a single fastest sample. That paired
thread check remains unperformed; the dispatch profile below is complete.

## Observed CPU grouped-query dispatch

The [typed profiler](../../benchmarks/analysis/torch/profile.py) froze the first
eight canonical cases, their numerical reference, and eleven source files before
loading. It used FP32 CPU, eight intra-op threads, inter-op twelve, batch eight,
maximum length 512 and cache zero. One warmup preceded two ordinary calls and
two CPU-only shape profiles, with stack/memory tracing disabled. The
[receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-profile8.json),
[incremental raw cycles](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-profile8.cycles.jsonl)
and [wall receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-profile8.wall.json)
retain outputs, operators, shapes, self times and process observations.
The owned process completed in 6.386 seconds within its 180-second cap.

Both profiles observed exactly 28 calls to
`aten::_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention_for_cpu`, with query shape
`[8,16,192,128]` and key/value shapes `[8,8,192,128]`. Neither recorded a math
SDPA fallback or explicit K/V repetition. This directly establishes grouped
CPU flash dispatch for the sampled workload. The installed Transformers helper
uses availability flags without inspecting the tensors' device: here its MPS
flag was false, and its no-mask/head-dimension branch enabled GQA. The matching
Torch CPU selector supports FP32 and grouped heads; its source eligibility is
consistent with the observed dispatch. An explicit-repeat-K/V alternative has
no demonstrated dispatch problem to fix and was not tested.

| Operator group | Profile 1 self time | Profile 2 self time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backbone matrix multiplications | 441.26 ms | 442.80 ms |
| MLP gate/up/down subset | 263.72 ms | 263.38 ms |
| CPU flash SDPA | 50.20 ms | 50.41 ms |
| All recorded operator self times | 582.58 ms | 585.30 ms |

These rows use self time, avoiding nested inclusive-time double counting. The
MLP row is a subset of the backbone row, not an additional cost. Backbone
matrix operations account for about 75.7% of the recorded self-time denominator;
MLP operations account for 45.1%, and flash SDPA accounts for 8.61%. Those are
profile diagnostics, not independently measured ordinary fractions or DRAM
bandwidth. Eliminating attention alone would have only a roughly `1.09x`
conditional Amdahl ceiling under these diagnostic fractions, well below `20x`.

All forty warmup/control/profile outputs matched the frozen logits and
probabilities exactly, preserving every selection and complete ranking.
Accuracy was seven of eight for each call, with unknown Kai training exposure.
Ordinary call times were 617.60 and 638.12 ms; profiled call times were 594.60
and 596.34 ms. The median ratio of `0.948` does not establish a profiler
speedup: controls ran before profiles, and two observations cannot separate
order, warm-state or observer effects. Profile outer times including capture
setup/teardown were 614.91 and 612.47 ms. No production attention switch or
performance improvement claim follows from this diagnostic.

## Completed FP32 gate/up packing

The experiment-only [candidate](../../benchmarks/analysis/torch/packing.py)
concatenates exact gate/up weights into one maintained `Linear`, then preserves
the activation, elementwise product and down projection. It shares unchanged
backbone parameters through distinct module dictionaries; it does not mutate
the baseline or add a production inference path. Both assays used the same
77 cases, eight threads, cache zero, one warmup and five alternating pairs.

| Batch size | Paired median | Paired p05 | Throughput, baseline → packed | Median gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 1.02047x | 1.01334x | 13.439 → 13.695 requests/s | Pass |
| 1 | 1.01494x | 1.01058x | 8.248 → 8.365 requests/s | Fail |

The unchanged performance gate requires median >=1.02, p05 >1, higher
throughput and no cohort p95 regression. All 1,078 outputs per assay passed
the frozen reference gates, with every selection/ranking preserved and 67/77
correct in every cohort. Maximum logit drift was `9.537e-7` at batch eight and
`1.431e-6` at batch one. Batch eight passed locally; scalar inference missed
the original threshold. The candidate is rejected for production promotion
under the required two-shape confirmation. The roughly 2% local result is not
a portable speed guarantee.

The [batch-eight receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-packing77.json)
and [scalar receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-packing77-b1.json)
retain raw outputs, paired cycles, diagnostics, source archives and parent
wall receipts. Both processes exited zero within their caps: 83.216 and
133.715 seconds respectively. Independent review reconstructed the gates and
raw evidence. Historical receipts and executed source archives remain intact.

## Completed frozen one-projection max-autotune probe

The separate [probe](../../benchmarks/analysis/torch/autotune.py) captured the
first real batch's layer-zero gate input `[1536,1024]` and exact FP32 weight
`[3072,1024]`. It compiled only that private maintained `Linear`, with freezing,
one compiler thread and a private cache. Cold compile plus first call took
3.045 seconds; the whole owned process took 7.129 seconds under its 120-second
cap. The local projection-only additive `torch.allclose` gate is distinct
from the complete-model quality gate. All retained projection outputs were
bit-identical, but that establishes neither full-model quality nor a speed gain.

Autotune selected ATen `mm` on the Accelerate-enabled build: 3.1288 ms versus
9.9839 ms for the proposed NEON CPP alternative. Generated code called
`extern_kernels.mm`. Five alternating warm pairs gave median `0.98404x`, with
ratios spanning 0.863–1.161. No full-model max-autotune or production compile
switch follows. These observations do not identify an internal Accelerate or
AMX microkernel.

The [receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-autotune-projection.json)
and [dispatch sidecar](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-autotune-projection.dispatch.json)
retain timings, actual selection/code excerpts, log hash and numerical archive
hash. The raw tensor archive includes model weights and stays local, excluded
from Git and source distributions. The supervisor kills and reaps its owned
process group on completion or timeout; independent testing verified cleanup
of a real child and sleeping descendant. No compiler descendants remained.

## Maintained CPU prefix screen

Read-only inspection of installed Transformers 5.18 supports a narrow
experiment with maintained `Qwen3Model` and `DynamicCache`, full final block
unchanged. Prefill the exact 25 tokens once, retain detached private FP32 K/V
snapshots and construct a fresh `DynamicCache(ddp_cache_data=..., config=...)`
per call from batch-expanded snapshots. Its `DynamicLayer.update` concatenates
into new storage, so suffix writes need not mutate shared prefix tensors.
Do not reuse a growing cache between requests. Check storage independence and
unchanged snapshots in tiny repeated/interleaved-call tests before a real run.

The current model derives RoPE positions from cache length; a seeded prefix
therefore starts suffix positions at 25. Candidate/query readouts become their
original positions minus 25. A mismatched prefix, empty suffix or any readout
inside the prefix requires whole-batch fallback. Preserve full input admission,
candidate order and exact token segmentation.

For multi-token suffixes, maintained mask construction creates an explicit
offset causal mask: key position <= suffix query position + 25. Plain rectangular
`is_causal=True` has the wrong alignment. Removing this mask is unsafe; the
current integration can additionally slice K/V for an unmasked rectangular
causal invocation. [PyTorch SDPA contract](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention.html)

The earlier sandbox MPS availability flag was false. With that flag, the
maintained masked-attention helper repeats K/V heads and does not pass
`enable_gqa=True`. A later read-only native Mac probe found both Torch MPS
availability and the helper's MPS flag true: with Torch >=2.13, maintained
masked CPU GQA can be admitted naturally. Freeze that native execution context
for both arms; do not patch global flags. The pinned CPU selector accepts
supported masks and grouped heads, but real-model masked suffix dispatch,
repetition cost and complete gain remain unknown.
[Maintained integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huggingface/transformers/v5.18.0/src/transformers/integrations/sdpa_attention.py),
[pinned CPU selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/5c4886908584029761b579af026dcfb627c84070/aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/sdp_utils_cpp.cpp)

The prepared prospective screen is first-eight real cases, FP32/eight threads,
batch eight/cache zero, unchanged full-block/head baseline and exact prefix
tokens. Freeze source/reference and log availability flags; retain one warmup
and two ordinary controls per arm, then one CPU shape profile per arm. Strict
original quality gates and actual Q16/KV8 flash head shapes admit the full
experiment; the two-control timing ratio is descriptive. Preserve mask shapes,
flash/math operators and self times.
Include fresh-cache construction in ordinary timing; record eager prefix build
time/memory separately. Only a passing screen justifies full-77 five-pair timing
and separate scalar confirmation under the original performance thresholds.
The typed candidate and screen live in `benchmarks/analysis/torch/prefix/`; tiny tests
challenge full-model parity, future-token causality, exact offset masks,
interleaved cache ownership, ragged order, whole-batch fallback and admission.
The independently reviewed command ran in the released native compute window:

```sh
python -m benchmarks.analysis.torch.prefix.run .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --output benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix8.json
```

The [first-eight receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix8.json)
retains eight cycles and 64 raw outputs. Every strict numerical, selection and
full-ranking gate passed against the frozen CPU reference; accuracy was 7/8
in every cycle. Maximum prefix logit drift was `6.080e-6` and probability drift
`7.618e-7`. The owned process exited zero in 7.945 seconds, without timeout;
the previously reviewed source bytes remained unchanged.

Both profiles observed 28 CPU flash calls and no math fallback. Full-prefill
queries were `[8,16,192,128]`; suffix queries were `[8,16,167,128]`. Both used
K/V `[8,8,192,128]`, establishing unexpanded GQA. The suffix profile retained
the explicit mask `[8,1,167,192]`. Native HF MPS availability and Torch >=2.13
flags were true without patching; eligibility alone was not used as dispatch
evidence.

Ordinary full-prefill controls took 607.30/599.84 ms and prefix controls took
555.24/545.24 ms, a descriptive median ratio `1.09692x`. Profile/ordinary ratios
were 1.000 and 1.010 respectively; one profile per arm cannot establish observer
effects. Prefix construction took 67.12 ms and retained 5,734,400 logical bytes.
Observed FP32 K/V shapes imply 352,321,536 bytes for the candidate's 28 extended
cache layers during one batch-eight call, excluding temporary copies. The
uncached baseline does not retain that stack. RSS counters are cumulative shared
process high water, not per-engine live memory or separate peak estimates.

This dispatch/quality screen admitted the separately reviewed confirmations
below. The two-control ratio remains descriptive and is not their verdict.

## Full77 CPU prefix confirmation

Maintained prefix reuse passed the independently reconstructed batch-eight and
scalar confirmations on the native M4 Pro. The
[batch-eight receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix77-b8.json),
[scalar receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix77-b1.json) and
[independent combined audit](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix77-review.json)
retain raw outcomes, all pairs, source identities and terminal wall receipts.
At this historical confirmation, the candidate remained experiment-only while
cache resource lifetime was evaluated. The subsequent comparison below retained
this ownership, and the [final-source opt-in CPU scorer](cpu/prefix.md) now has
its own independently audited confirmation. These earlier receipts remain
unchanged.

| Batch | Paired median | Paired p05 | Throughput, full → prefix | Cohort p95 ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 1.10097x | 1.09393x | 13.316 → 14.664 requests/s | 0.90220 |
| 1 | 1.07610x | 1.07442x | 8.275 → 8.909 requests/s | 0.92872 |

Both shapes used all 77 frozen cases, FP32 CPU/eight threads, max length 512,
cache zero and the same exact 25-token prefix, with the full final block intact.
Each retained two screens, one warmup per arm and five alternating measured
pairs. Before either full77 result, the CPU confirmation explicitly strengthened
its prospective performance gate: median >=1.02, paired p05 >1, aggregate
throughput ratio >1 and no cohort p95 regression. All four passed for both
shapes. These four conditions do not rewrite the earlier MLX protocol.

All 2,156 screen/warmup/measured outputs passed the frozen CPU reference gates:
every selection and complete ranking agreed, with no failures and 67/77 correct
in every cohort. Maximum prefix logit/probability drift was `9.835e-6`/`1.543e-6`
at batch eight and `9.954e-6`/`1.560e-6` at batch one. Repetitions do not add
independent quality cases; Kai's exposure to this training-source cohort is
unknown. Five-pair quantiles describe these observations, not confidence bounds.

Prefix construction took 69.01 ms and 67.70 ms respectively, outside ordinary
inference. Every fresh per-call cache allocation/copy stayed inside measured
latency. Both runs retained the same 5,734,400-byte immutable prefix snapshots;
extended and temporary K/V allocations are additional. No per-engine physical
memory saving is established by the shared cumulative RSS counters.

Both owned processes exited zero without timeout, in 80.54 and 129.28 seconds
under separate 180-second caps. The identical 17-file source archive digest is
`d86eb841ae184bbb6413418a86c542dc668eb14a310292b9cecfa1cfc3faeb31`.
`cache.py` remained byte-identical to the passing first-eight candidate. The
confirmation admitted that complete audited first-eight history, model/data/
reference/source identities and full token/readout vectors before measurement.
Production code did not change.

The next proposal at confirmation time was a first-eight comparison of this
retained cache against a separately proved one-use owner. That resource screen
is now completed below; the earlier tiny proof established mechanics only.

## One-use CPU cache resource screen

Three fresh serial native M4 Pro process pairs supported the predeclared
resource hypothesis. The [independent audit](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix-memory-review.json)
reconstructs all six child receipts, journals, source archives and owned wall
caps. No production code changed, and no inference speed gain is established.

| Pair | Retained sampled RSS, MB | One-use sampled RSS, MB | Signed reduction, MB | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 4421.55 | 4000.14 | 421.41 | 9.53% |
| 1 | 4422.80 | 3997.79 | 425.00 | 9.61% |
| 2 | 4428.12 | 3999.73 | 428.39 | 9.67% |

MB means 1,000,000 bytes. Each pair exceeded the prospective reduction threshold
`max(64 MiB, 5% retained sampled peak)` and had lower directly observed selected
K/V storage. These are inference-body **sampled current RSS** contrasts, not
whole-run or host peak memory measurements. The two arms shared a new private
scoring path with `use_cache=False` and kept their cache owner through the head;
only the maintained cache factory/reference lifetime differed. Tiny independent
checks also compared this path with the earlier `use_cache=True` retained scorer.

Each child used the frozen first eight cases, FP32 CPU/eight threads, batch eight,
max length 512, token cache zero, default RoPE, exact 25-token prefix and unchanged
full final block. Its screen, warmup, two ordinary controls, separate sampled
memory cycle and final shape profile retained 48 outcomes. All 288 outputs
passed the frozen CPU numerical, probability, full-ranking and selection gates,
with 7/8 correct each cycle and no failures. They represent eight unique
training-source cases; checkpoint exposure remains unknown. Every profile
observed 28 CPU flash calls, zero math calls, Q16/KV8 heads and the correct
`[8,1,167,192]` offset mask, without changing backend flags.

All 174 storage observations matched the independent allocation formulas.
The selected union of persistent prefix snapshots, current cache-owned K/V and
locally returned K/V peaked at 358,055,936 bytes retained versus 62,554,112 bytes
one-use. Aliased views count their backing storage once; returned tensors remain
counted after cache reset. This boundary excludes suffix projection inputs,
in-concatenation overlap, other activations/workspaces and allocator arenas.
Storage bytes are not RSS, and the larger RSS contrast cannot be attributed
solely to these selected tensors.

RSS sampling retained 21–22 valid interior queries per child, with conservative
maximum body gaps 49.28–50.84 ms, below the frozen 100 ms bound; no observer errors,
limits or missing inventories occurred. Brief peaks can still be missed. The
intrusive memory cycle took 1.48–1.54 times the same child's ordinary median;
query latency and all raw gaps remain recorded. Profiles followed sampling,
and post-profile current RSS was higher than the sampled body peak in every
child. Cold load, warm snapshots and cumulative high-water RSS remain distinct;
none substitutes for sampled current RSS. Ordinary timings are descriptive.

Prefix construction took 69.09–72.75 ms outside inference; each call included
fresh cache construction/copying. All six owned children exited zero in
6.76–6.90 seconds under separate 180-second caps and were reaped. Source bytes
and prior first-eight/full77 receipts remained unchanged through the runs.

The proposed next validation was separate full77 batch-eight and scalar
comparison through existing `benchmark_pair`. That confirmation is completed
below; the resource screen alone did not select a CPU cache owner.

## One-use full77 latency confirmation

One-use ownership failed its predeclared selection gates against retained prefix
reuse at both batch sizes. It preserved quality and the existing speed benefit
over full prefill. The [independent four-comparison audit](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-one-use-latency-review.json)
reconstructs every raw result, source/history identity and terminal wall receipt.
Reject one-use selection; production remains unchanged.

| Comparator | Batch | Paired median | Paired p05 | Aggregate throughput ratio | Cohort p95 ratio | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Retained prefix | 8 | 0.999794x | 0.996876x | 1.000906 | 1.001281 | Reject selection |
| Retained prefix | 1 | 1.001429x | 0.998753x | 1.003504 | 0.988835 | Reject selection |
| Original full prefill | 8 | 1.109282x | 1.088292x | 1.103699 | 0.918216 | Pass original gates |
| Original full prefill | 1 | 1.073133x | 1.058034x | 1.068196 | 0.942890 | Pass original gates |

Both comparator policies were declared before any timing: retained-prefix
selection required median >=1, paired p05 >1, aggregate throughput >1 and
cohort p95 ratio <=1. Full-prefill confirmation preserved the original median
>=1.02 with the same other three conditions. Batch eight failed retained median,
p05 and tail conditions; scalar failed retained p05. These observations are near
parity, but do not pass the fixed selection policy. The independently supported
9.53–9.67% sampled RSS reduction does not compensate for a failed latency gate.
Separate full-prefill results cannot establish improvement over retained reuse.

Each fresh native M4 Pro job used all 77 pinned cases, FP32 CPU/eight threads,
max length 512, token cache zero, exact 25-token prefix and full final block.
Canonical `benchmark_pair` retained one warmup per arm and five alternating
pairs: 12 complete cycles and 924 strict outputs per job, with no separate
pre-screen. Every one of the 3,696 outputs passed frozen legacy CPU logit,
probability, complete-ranking and selection checks, with 67/77 correct each
cycle and no failures. There are 77 unique training-source cases, not 3,696
independent quality cases; checkpoint exposure is unknown. Five-pair quantiles
are observations, not confidence bounds.

The shared retained and one-use scoring paths differed only in their private
cache factory/lifetime. The full comparator used the original unwrapped
`KaiScorer`. Cold prefix construction stayed outside timing; fresh per-call
cache construction/copies, encoding, model, host values and decision processing
stayed inside. No profiler, RSS sampler or tensor-storage observer ran.

The jobs completed in 66.53, 110.55, 69.33 and 114.32 seconds under separate
180-second caps. The two retained comparisons exited one for valid completed
negative selections; the full-prefill jobs exited zero. None timed out, and all
owned groups were reaped. All 23 frozen source files, complete memory/prior77
histories and model/data/reference identities passed admission and final audit.
The canonical benchmark returns raw cycles only on completion: setup was saved
before the call and all returned rows before gate calculations; a timeout would
leave internal partial timing and quality unknown. No retry, source or threshold
change followed the negative results.

## Maintained guidance and boundaries

PyTorch's current [`set_num_threads`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.set_num_threads.html)
API controls intra-operation CPU parallelism and recommends configuring it
before eager/JIT/autograd work. [`set_num_interop_threads`](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.set_num_interop_threads.html)
is a different process-global control that may be set only once before inter-op
work. The old TorchScript threading page now contains a deprecation warning;
these explicit APIs are better current references. Library scorers should not
change process-wide counts per request. A dedicated benchmark process can
change intra-op counts between arms; keep inter-op fixed and record both values.

The installed-build [OpenMP setter](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/5c4886908584029761b579af026dcfb627c84070/aten/src/ATen/ParallelOpenMP.cpp)
updates OpenMP and, when compiled, MKL/QNNPACK pools. It contains no
Accelerate-specific worker-limit call. Therefore the experiment's axis is the
configured ATen intra-op count, not a claim that every BLAS operation uses
exactly that many workers. Record environment variables and
`torch.__config__.parallel_info()` per arm; do not invent an Accelerate affinity
policy. [PyTorch's environment-variable guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/threading_environment_variables.html)
describes OpenMP/MKL controls, while its
[tuning guide](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/recipes/recipes/tuning_guide.html)
contains platform-specific affinity advice. Linux NUMA binding and Intel runtime
preload examples do not establish a Mac optimization.

On a later oneDNN-capable wheel, availability and actual dispatched operators
must be observed first. Internal BF16/TF32 computation can be selected for
FP32 tensors, so tensor dtype alone does not establish strict FP32 arithmetic.
Keep the supported IEEE computation policy and declare precision metadata.
The official speed examples are Intel SPR observations, not this Mac's ceiling.
[MKLDNN precision controls](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/notes/mkldnn.html)

The installed-build [CPU SDPA selector](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/5c4886908584029761b579af026dcfb627c84070/aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/sdp_utils_cpp.cpp)
prioritizes CPU flash attention when dtype/shape/stride/dropout guards pass,
then math. It includes FP32 and grouped-query support. A profile must establish
which kernel this full-model invocation reaches; generic CUDA FlashAttention
advice is insufficient. Different fused kernels may change reductions.
[SDPA accuracy guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention.html)

Shape compilation can specialize guards, recompile on changed shapes or fall
back to eager after cache limits. `TORCH_LOGS=recompiles,graph_breaks` can explain
a *new* concrete compilation hypothesis; dynamic shapes are not a promised
speedup. The completed warm regression is not explained merely by cold compile
cost, and increasing cache limits or adding padding would require fresh evidence.
[Recompilation guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/user_guide/torch_compiler/compile/programming_model.recompilation.html)

## Completed bounded experiment protocol

The tested hypothesis was: on the unchanged FP32/SDPA Kai artifact, a count among
`1,2,4,6,8,12` improves complete cohort throughput over eight threads without
changing logits beyond `atol=rtol=1e-3`, probabilities beyond `1e-4`, any
selection or any complete ranking. This affects backbone-wide scheduling;
its scope exceeds head-only work without adding an inference implementation.
The sampled counts did not improve on eight; interpolation remains unknown.

Freeze all 77 cases, canonical order, batch size eight, exact padded lengths,
max length 512, no token cache, no compilation, no autocast and one loaded
scorer. Check artifact/reference/dataset hashes and exact tokens/endpoints before
timing. Hold inter-op count and environment constant. Warm every count once,
then collect six cycles per count in rotating orders so every count occupies
each position exactly once. Every cycle includes tokenization, packing, forward,
host materialization and decision interpretation; exclude setup, warmup, receipt
serialization, HTTP and admission queues. Preserve all raw rows and failures.
Intra-op changes are benchmark process state, recorded explicitly per arm.

The typed runner is `benchmarks/analysis/torch/threads.py`:

```sh
python -m benchmarks.analysis.torch.threads .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --output benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-threads77.json
```

The thin runner reuses Wyat's synchronous benchmark cycles, failure-inclusive
quality comparison, shared frozen-input checks and pure scaling fit. Focused
pytest/Hypothesis checks establish balanced orders, rejection of input drift,
thread-state restoration after load failure and timeout failure reporting;
these checks do not execute model inference.

Before model loading, the runner captures the declared source files once into
a content-addressed, exclusive-create UTF-8 source archive beside the receipt.
Its final source hashes come from that frozen snapshot, rather than re-reading
files after measurement. This preserves setup source bytes across team edits;
it does not prove external dependency identity or archive model checkpoints.
The frozen numerical-reference hash is also retained from setup.

Each warmup and measured cycle carries before/after wall and monotonic times,
own-process cumulative user/system CPU time, minor/major faults, voluntary and
involuntary context switches, and OS load averages. These lightweight reads and
receipt writes occur outside `_run`'s timed interval. Snapshot collection time
is recorded separately; unavailable OS load is explicit. Counter differences
may challenge an outlier hypothesis but do not identify its cause. OS load
does not reveal a competing task's identity or GPU utilization.
The shared helper accepts optional device-memory counters supplied by the GPU
runner's owner; it imports no GPU framework. Those counters must name active,
cached and peak bytes separately, rather than treating a cumulative peak as
current usage. The GPU probe also belongs outside the measured interval.

Use a 600-second experiment wall cap with incremental flushed cycle receipts;
a timeout retains partial evidence and cannot become a pass. A winning screen
needs a separate paired confirmation against eight threads; report variation
and failed runs instead of selecting one fastest sample. This fixed-batch sweep
is distinct from the concurrently owned MLX batch-size sweep.

After ordinary measurements, capture at most two representative warmed batches
with CPU profiler activity and shape recording, without stack or memory tracing.
Keep an unprofiled control. Look for Linear `mm/addmm`, SDPA CPU flash versus
math, copies/repeated K/V, norms and host encoding. Shape tracing can retain
tensors, create extra copies and add overhead, so profile fractions are
conditional diagnostics rather than ordinary latency evidence.
[Profiler contract](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/profiler.html)
Do not sum nested operator inclusive times. External Accelerate worker topology
and actual DRAM traffic remain unknown from an ATen table alone.

USL fits are descriptive here: heterogeneous cores, hidden BLAS worker policies
and finite small load range limit a physical processor interpretation. Keep
unconstrained estimates, residuals and warnings; invalid or weak fits are
inconclusive. An Amdahl ceiling requires a measured affected fraction, and a
roofline bound requires justified traffic and device throughput limits.
Neither a fitted coefficient nor this measured sweep establishes a 20× CPU gain.

# Explicit CPU prefix reuse: final-source confirmation

The hypothesis is that exposing the previously tested retained-prefix recipe as
an explicit CPU scorer preserves its numerical behavior and saves at least 2%
of complete inference time at batch one and batch eight. The earlier experimental
results support this test; they do not validate newly moved production code.
Default loading and CLI behavior retain full prefill. The shared tensor core
preserves the ordinary forward arguments and CUDA precision policy.

The programmatic entry point is
`wyat.backends.kai.cpu.prefix.PrefixScorer`; install the `inference` extra for
CPU use and the `server` extra when serving it. It implements the existing
scorer contract:

```python
from wyat import Candidate, Model, Request
from wyat.backends.kai.cpu.prefix import PrefixScorer
from wyat.backends.kai.torch import KaiScorer
from wyat.server import create_app

base = KaiScorer.from_directory("/models/kai", device="cpu")
example = Request(
    context="Classify customer banking support requests into the supplied intents.",
    query="I have a missing refund",
    candidates=(Candidate("refund", "Missing refund"), Candidate("card", "Card problem")),
)
scorer = PrefixScorer(base, base.encode_request(example).ids[:25])
model = Model(scorer, scorer.model_id)
decision = model.decide(example)
app = create_app(model)
```

Choose the exact token prefix shared by the intended inputs; 25 is an explicit
choice in this example, not an automatic policy. Matching text alone does not
establish matching tokens. This CPU path retains the complete final block.

The candidate owns one eagerly prepared immutable token prefix for a fixed
CPU FP32, eval-mode, full-attention Kai model with default unscaled RoPE and SDPA.
Every call gets fresh maintained cache owners; suffix state does not survive the
call. Original complete inputs are encoded and admitted before prefix removal.
A mismatch, empty suffix or readout inside the prefix falls back for the entire
batch. Keep weights, head, configuration, device and encoder fixed for the
resource lifetime. There is no automatic prefix policy or process-wide precision,
thread or attention-policy change in the scorer.
Ambient CPU autocast and backbone forward hooks are outside this resource's
equivalence contract and are rejected. The constructor checks the maintained cache's
capabilities before prefix computation. Required cache and position APIs are
present in the declared minimum
[Transformers 5.17 cache implementation](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.17.0/src/transformers/cache_utils.py)
and [Qwen3 forward](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.17.0/src/transformers/models/qwen3/modeling_qwen3.py).
Source-level API presence does not establish numerical or performance results on
every allowed runtime version.

## Prospective protocol

Use the existing pinned Kai release and all 77 ordered training-source BANKING77
development menus, with their original six choices, tokens and readout positions.
The dataset SHA256 is
`0020d9a3c72a21941ba551cf31f404187f69c6a5dc30299cc0a24d303b904a03`;
the legacy CPU reference SHA256 is
`b8a90b31941b60e793357a8cb360767520da70ec33d2161c1242606962b22664`.
The ordered input digest is
`fd5dd942250c6416c4ab50c59a5164a20909d11ead12bf83c505efff6a5556e8`.
Reserved confirmation remains closed; prior model exposure is unknown.

Run two separate fresh native Mac processes, B8 and B1, each under the existing
180-second owned-worker cap. Use eight intraop threads, FP32 CPU SDPA,
max_length=512, token_cache_size=0 and the exact common 25-token prefix.
Retain installed runtime versions, Torch build and unchanged native HF masked-GQA
eligibility flags. The flags are a condition for this performance comparison,
not a universal correctness requirement for CPU prefix caching.

Within each process, share one freshly loaded base between full prefill and the
final prefix scorer. Run a screen and warmup for each arm, then five measured
pairs in AB, BA, AB, BA, AB order. Retain all fourteen chronological cohorts,
1,078 outcomes per shape, including failures and partial histories. B8 retains
nine batches of eight and the final five; B1 retains all 77 scalar calls.

Compare every output with the frozen legacy CPU reference and measured paired
arms using the existing gates: logits satisfy the existing 1e-3 absolute/relative
comparison, probabilities differ by at most 1e-4, every full rank and selection
agrees, and no failure, missing prediction or labeled-accuracy loss occurs.
No tolerance changes follow an observed result.

Use complete `_run` cohort latency, including per-call cache construction,
packing, computation and host output materialization. Preparation is measured
separately. Source hashing, diagnostics, journals and profiling stay outside the
timed body; no intrusive memory sampler is introduced. All four existing speed
gates must pass at both shapes:

- paired median speedup >= 1.02;
- sample p05 paired speedup > 1;
- aggregate baseline/candidate time ratio > 1;
- candidate/baseline cohort p95 time ratio <= 1.

Freeze final source and relevant installed dependency source before execution;
check stability outside each timed cohort and afterward. Validate historical
receipts against their immutable executed archives, rather than requiring the
current checkout to remain identical to old code. Independently reconstruct
raw outcomes, scheduling, quality and performance metrics before promotion.

The connected first-eight, full77 and memory-history admissions now check each
archived source's text hash and complete inventory against its pinned execution
receipt. Their original receipt, journal, wall, review and archive hash constants
remain unchanged. They no longer read live Python files to identify an old run.
When those tools execute a new experiment, they separately archive its current
source. Focused tests challenge the boundary by forbidding live source reads
during historical admission; all numerical and performance rules retain their
original meaning.

## Observed final-source results

The first-eight screen passed 48 outputs, followed by separate full77 B8 and B1
confirmations. Independent standard-library audits reconstructed all 2,204 raw
outcomes, complete ranks, numerical gates and chronological pairs, and validated
source archives and terminal worker receipts. The audits validated frozen
reference token vectors, prefix/readout geometry and recorded input lengths;
exact fresh runtime encoding was attested by the source-frozen runner rather
than independently retokenized. Every full cohort retains 67/77
correct selections, with no missing prediction or failure. The screen carries
no performance verdict.

| Batch | Paired median speedup | Paired p05 | Aggregate speedup | Candidate/baseline cohort p95 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 1.10038x | 1.09290x | 1.09870x | 0.91436 |
| 1 | 1.07260x | 1.01150x | 1.06265x | 0.97340 |

All four predeclared performance gates pass at both shapes. The five B8 pair
ratios are 1.09220, 1.09573, 1.10115, 1.10038 and 1.10415. The B1 ratios are
1.07794, 1.06546, 1.07260, **0.99801** and 1.10493: one scalar pair regresses
about 0.20%. The interpolated sample p05 passes the original gate; it is not a
confidence bound or a claim that every future pair improves. These complete
cohort timings include fresh cache owners, packing, model computation and host
output materialization.

Maximum logit/probability drift is 9.835e-6/1.543e-6 at B8 and
9.954e-6/1.560e-6 at B1, within the unchanged strict gates. Prefix construction
took 69.968 ms and 70.082 ms respectively, separately from inference. Both
resources retain 5,734,400 logical prefix bytes; extended and temporary K/V
allocations are additional. The first-eight, B8 and B1 workers exited zero and
were reaped in 7.964, 83.275 and 135.724 seconds under separate 180-second caps.
Thread settings were restored before each successful completion was recorded.

The [first-eight audit](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix-production-first8-review.json),
[B8 audit](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix-production77-b8-review.json)
and [B1 audit](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-prefix-production77-b1-review.json)
retain exact raw receipt hashes and independent calculations. All three runs
share executed source archive SHA256
`22aa511fe5434b21aa6b6d45c0d6cbe42ef71473d53dc0ceddec202bd0e9e409`.
Those immutable archives describe the executed code and protocol; this summary
was updated after the audits.

## Connected checks and limits

The complete native CPU/Metal and actual DMBench regression passed 971 tests,
zero skips and one existing Starlette/httpx deprecation warning. Strict mypy
passed on 146 maintained sources; Ruff lint and formatting passed. The owned
pytest child exited and was reaped in 28.669 seconds under its 120-second cap.
All source bytes stayed stable. The initial full check found a duplicate test
basename at collection; the unchanged test was renamed, and that failed receipt
remains alongside the successful
[final regression](../../../benchmarks/real/engine-cpu-prefix-production-verification-final.json).
Current-source native CUDA execution is unmeasured; the existing CUDA receipts
describe their earlier frozen runtime.
These observations do not establish current peak RSS,
an allocation ceiling or a benefit for another prefix or workload. No HTTP
capacity, online latency, GPU gain, 20x speedup or held-out quality follows from
this assay. The existing scorer interface permits an explicitly constructed
resource to be used by `Model` and the server without a separate transport path.

files.text:
# CPU projection packing primitive

The hypothesis is that one maintained FP32 linear operation for K/V or Q/K/V
reduces layer-zero projection cost. This is a primitive test, before a whole-model
candidate. Numerical and full-ranking model parity remain hard constraints.

The existing captured gate inputs are post-attention MLP activations and are not
QKV inputs. Instead, read the exact released checkpoint through Safetensors mmap:
only the required embedding rows, layer-zero input RMSNorm and Q/K/V weights.
Apply maintained Qwen3RMSNorm with epsilon `1e-6` to the authoritative full token
vectors, then take suffix rows after the exact 25-token prefix. This norm is
per-token; preceding attention is absent in layer zero. No backbone is created or
executed. Pinned tokenizer metadata resolves padding to token `151643`.

The four fixed operands are canonical offsets 7/18/75 (full lengths 192/197/214,
suffix lengths 167/172/189) and the canonical first eight requests, padded to 192
before normalization and prefix removal (B8 suffix length 167). Preserve token
IDs, case IDs, ordering, padding, activation bytes, shapes and strides. All 77
reference vectors and canonical inputs are admitted before checkpoint tensors.
These are BANKING77 training-source development cases; checkpoint exposure is
unknown.

Q/K/V have output widths 2048/1024/1024 and input width 1024. One FP32 packed
allocation is 16 MiB. Separate Q/K/V use contiguous views; packed KV uses its
contiguous tail; packed QKV uses the complete allocation. Original source tensors
are released after exact-bit checks. The temporary source-plus-packed projection
pool is 32 MiB during setup, excluding normalization, activations, output archives
and allocator storage. This is logical capacity, not RSS. Hypothetical 28-layer
QKV and KV copies would be 448/224 MiB if originals were also retained; this
primitive does not create those copies.

Every arm executes one cold call, one warm call and six measured calls, following
all six permutations of `separate`, `kv`, `qkv`: 96 total calls across four
operands. The clock contains one `project()` call, including admission, maintained
`F.linear` and output splitting. Setup, hashing, snapshots, quality comparisons
and persistence occur outside that clock. Each call's output shapes, strides,
bytes hash and raw timing are retained before its gate can reject it. Save each
distinct output and input in an excluded local Safetensors artifact. Changed
strides may affect later Q/K normalization or RoPE; neither is timed here.

Projection parity uses the original symmetric max allowance:
`abs(a-b) <= max(1e-3, 1e-3 * max(abs(a), abs(b)))`, with finite FP32 outputs.
There is no probability or full-ranking claim at this boundary. The unchanged
whole-model gates remain mandatory for any later candidate.

A candidate is eligible for a later full-model screen only if all four operands
have six-order median baseline/candidate ratio at least **1.12** and interpolated
sample p05 strictly above **1.0**. This prospective filter is not promotion. A
historical profiled projection fraction of 0.1938 motivates conservative triage
under an unchanged-cost assumption; it is not an observed ordinary fraction or
speed bound. Every ratio remains visible, including regressions. Source/assets,
process policy and thread restoration must pass before a positive completion
receipt. No new precision policy, JIT, GPU work or production changes occur.

The command below records the historical launch. Existing receipts must remain
intact; any separately authorized repeat requires a fresh output stem. No repeat
is needed or authorized by these results.

```sh
python -m benchmarks.analysis.torch.projection.run .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --output benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive.json
```

The standard-library parent owns one 120-second child process group. Timeout,
failed output, missing call or incomplete receipt is unknown/rejected; do not
rerun or relax gates to hide it. Local primitive timings cannot establish a model,
server or general CPU speed gain. No production promotion is performed.

## Observed result

The repaired bounded worker completed **96 calls** across all four authentic
operands. The independent standard-library audit bound every saved output to its
actual FP32 array and recomputed the unchanged symmetric numerical gate. All
three arms have identical output hashes at every shape, with maximum absolute
and relative differences **zero**. Exact packed projection values match the
released layer-zero Q/K/V tensors after their BF16-to-FP32 expansion.

| Authentic operand | KV median | KV sample p05 | QKV median | QKV sample p05 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scalar, full length 192 | 1.01678x | 0.93591x | 1.07154x | 1.01623x |
| Scalar, full length 197 | 1.02530x | 1.01108x | 1.05531x | 1.04202x |
| Scalar, full length 214 | 1.02920x | 1.00146x | 1.05988x | 1.03029x |
| First eight, padded full length 192 | 1.04164x | 1.00155x | 1.03274x | 0.96456x |

Both variants miss the prospective **1.12x median at every operand** condition.
KV also regresses in the scalar-192 tail, and QKV regresses in the batch-eight
tail. All six ratios per operand and arm remain in the
[raw report](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final.json)
and [independent audit](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final-review.json).
Both `primitive_eligible` values are false; `accepted` remains false. Do not
construct or promote a full-model candidate from this screen. This rejects the
measured packing candidate under this declared filter, without ruling out
another implementation or context. The sample p05 is not a confidence bound.

The inference child exited zero and was reaped after **4.122 s** within its
120-second cap. Source/asset verification and original thread restoration pass.
The independent audit exited zero and was reaped after **3.061 s** within its
separate 60-second cap; its
[execution receipt](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final-review-final.execution.json)
preserves exact producer text, argv, output and ownership. The audit validates
16 executed source texts, the six reviewed experiment files, unchanged
production22 and the pinned input/model assets. The raw report SHA is
`fe4d68337e4b695bdafc26c18ed261bd776175e36e6970ed03694965840afe17`;
the executed source archive SHA is
`eff85f9cc7c03a0d045499df4c984d9747e6c7c23d60efad53c841caf2b97fb6`.
The prospective protocol above remains in that immutable archive; this result
was appended afterward.

Normalized operands are authenticated by source/model/token provenance and
retained byte identities. The auditor does not independently replay Torch's
RMSNorm reduction or recompute every matrix product: separate-projection outputs
are its numerical parity oracle. Input outer strides retain the full-token
width for singleton batches, where that stride is inactive, and use the compact
suffix width for batch eight. Output split strides differ between arms and are
retained explicitly. Q/K normalization, RoPE, attention, cache updates, decision
heads, ranks and probabilities are outside this primitive. Logical allocation
counters do not establish RSS, peak memory, device aliases or whole-model speed.

## Preserved failure history

The initial real worker rejected its own supervisor-created `.wall.json` and
`.log` sidecars before input admission or checkpoint operands. It exited one
without a timeout after **1.799 s**; no main receipt or primitive sample exists.
That attempt is an execution-harness failure with unknown quality and speed.
Its [wall](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive.wall.json) and
[log](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive.log) remain intact.
A narrowly reviewed sidecar allowance plus collision tests preceded the fresh
final run; the repaired focused suite passed **18 tests**.

The first independent raw-audit attempt assumed compact outer input strides even
for singleton batches and stopped before output parity scans. Its
[failed execution receipt](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final-review.execution.json)
and exact producer remain preserved. The auditor then corrected only that
layout expectation and inspected the same immutable raw arrays successfully;
no model inference was repeated for this auditor correction.
