files.text:
# Native MLX bottlenecks and bounded hypotheses

Observed on an Apple M4 Pro, MLX 0.32.3 and MLX-LM 0.31.3, using the pinned
Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B artifact and 77 frozen BANKING77 training-source development
requests with six candidates each. This is a runtime and numerical assay;
checkpoint exposure to these examples is unknown. No gold label enters scoring.

The production path remains FP32 causal prefill followed by endpoint gathering
and the FP32 candidate head. Its maintained upstream Transformer is reused.
The model has 28 layers, hidden width 1024, intermediate width 3072, 16 query
heads and eight KV heads with head dimension 128. Query projection width is
2048; each K/V projection width is 1024.

## Stage profile

`benchmarks/analysis/mlx/profile.py` measures complete ordinary scoring separately
from diagnostics that fence and evaluate every stage. Token cache is disabled,
batch size is eight, and original request order and pad-to-eight packing remain.
All token IDs/endpoints match the stored CPU reference. All five ordinary and
three diagnostic repetitions pass logit/probability tolerances, complete rank,
selection and accuracy gates; raw scores and stage repetitions are retained in
`benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-profile77-b8.json`.

Ordinary complete latency has median **2799.95 ms**; its five repeats are
2799.80, 2798.25, 2814.79, 2799.95 and 2801.07 ms. Diagnostic complete median is
3308.73 ms, **18.17% higher**. Fences change dispatch and fusion opportunities,
so the stage account diagnoses candidates rather than establishing exact hot
production kernel fractions.

| Phase | Median complete-cohort stage ms | Share of summed stage medians |
|---|---:|---:|
| Attention, including projections/RoPE/SDPA | 1314.13 | 40.14% |
| MLP, including projections/SwiGLU | 1628.49 | 49.74% |
| Two layer norms | 140.89 | 4.30% |
| Two residual additions | 158.95 | 4.85% |
| Encoding | 14.45 | 0.44% |
| Embedding | 7.87 | 0.24% |
| Candidate head | 3.94 | 0.12% |
| Packing, final norm, gathering, materialization | 5.49 | 0.17% |

The fractions use **3274.22 ms**, the sum of per-phase medians, as denominator.
The difference from complete diagnostic median is 34.51 ms, or 1.04% of that
complete diagnostic median. Per-phase medians are not an exact additive
decomposition of one particular cycle. Using complete diagnostic median instead
gives attention 39.72% and MLP 49.22%; completely removing either would imply
conditional Amdahl ceilings of 1.659× and 1.969× respectively. These ceilings
assume the remaining work is unaffected and still apply only to the diagnostic
execution account.

An entire final Transformer block accounts for about 3.45% of measured stages.
Even eliminating it would give only about 1.036× under this account. Computing
only final endpoints can remove only part of that block, so it is a modest
candidate, behind projection packing across every layer. Removing encoding or
the head alone cannot approach a large end-to-end gain on this cohort.

## Work estimates and observable kernels

The runner records individual projection matrix shapes, dense FLOPs and a
single-read/write operand-size proxy. Configured projection work per layer is
`2*B*L*(H*(Q+2*KV)+Q*H+3*H*I)`. Attention dense work is
`4*B*query_heads*L²*head_dim`; an ideal triangular causal count is also retained.
Norm, activation, RoPE and softmax operations are excluded from those FLOPs.
The dense projection plus SDPA total is 13.729 TFLOP per 77-request cohort,
equivalent to a configured-work rate of 4.903 TFLOP/s at the ordinary median.
This is an arithmetic proxy, not measured instruction throughput.

The aggregate operand-size proxy is 65.271 GB. It assumes each listed matrix
operand is accessed once and does not account for cross-operation caching.
It is **not measured DRAM traffic** and must not be divided by latency to claim
attained external memory bandwidth. Likewise the entire embedding table is not
read for each lookup. Active/peak MLX allocator memory is 2.388 GB / 3.847 GB.
Hardware utilization and a compute-versus-bandwidth bottleneck remain unknown.

An actual short Xcode Metal System Trace was recorded for an owned Python
process. `mlx-metal-inventory.json` exports only that process's 34 compiled
shader names. It observes FP32 steel GEMM, FP32 causal attention at head
dimension 128, RMSNorm, RoPE and compiled SwiGLU kernels. Initial loading and
validation kernels also appear. Shader Timeline was disabled and Counter Set
was null; reliable warmed-inference markers were absent. Consequently neither
per-shader latency nor aggregate hot-inference utilization is attributed from
this capture.

The raw 67 MB `.trace` bundle and raw XML exports remain ignored locally because
the template also collects incidental host process inventory and GPU rendering
events. The reviewable TOC removes unrelated process inventory and device
name/UUID. The reviewable inventory filters by the owned process PID and records
raw-export hashes without exposing unrelated events.

## Packing experiment

`benchmarks/analysis/mlx/fusion.py` tests QKV only, gate/up only and both against
the unchanged baseline. It concatenates immutable FP32 weights once and checks
every concatenated segment equals its source. Replaced modules retain no
reference to the old projection modules; the separate baseline retains those
weights for paired timing. The upstream norms, RoPE, native GQA SDPA, output and
down projections remain. The experimental attention explicitly rejects caches.

QKV packing reduces three projections to one, and gate/up packing reduces two
to one: 84 fewer projection dispatches across 28 layers, with unchanged configured
matrix arithmetic and stored weight values. Different GEMM shapes can still
change floating-point results, so each arm first receives a whole 77-request
quality gate against the stored CPU reference. Surviving arms receive five
alternating warmed complete-cohort pairs, with raw outputs retained. A batch 8
gain alone does not justify a universal default: scalar and scaling-best shape
confirmation is required. The batch-eight assay rejected this speed hypothesis:

| Arm | Median baseline/candidate speed | Paired p05–p95 | Quality |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| QKV | 0.98381× | 0.98243–0.98578× | pass |
| Gate/up | 0.99590× | 0.99130–0.99925× | pass |
| Both | 0.97610× | 0.81798–1.02156× | pass |

Each arm preserves every one of the 385 paired selections and complete rankings,
with bit-identical paired logits. Each first screen also passes the stored CPU
reference with max logit error 1.2875e-5. The combined arm's large variation is
retained; its cause is unknown. No packing change enters production.

Whole-process active allocator memory is 2.858, 3.563 and 4.737 GB for the
successive arms, with cumulative peak 6.659 GB. These controls retain baseline
weights and experimental objects through Python reference cycles; they do not
measure eventual production packed-model footprint. The retained runner now
releases reports and collects cycles outside timed calls between arms. The exact
executed runner is archived with a matching source hash in the receipt, and a
sidecar records these later verification/lifetime edits. A scalar shape experiment
would require its own declared hypothesis; batch-eight failure provides no
universal statement about all shapes.

Tiny pytest/Hypothesis mechanics checks pass on CPU and Metal (seven tests):
H16/Q32/KV16, varying endpoint count/length/right padding, all packing arms,
scalar-versus-batch causal parity, and explicit rejection of cache use.

## Endpoint-only final block hypothesis

`benchmarks/analysis/mlx/endpoints.py` retains the first maintained Transformer
blocks and every final-layer K/V row. Only Q, attention output, output projection,
MLP and final norm are evaluated at the ordered candidate/query endpoints.
The gathered residual is kept in that same order, including duplicate positions.
Each selected query becomes a one-token batch row for native RoPE, with its
original position supplied through the supported batch-offset array. Keys use
ordinary full-sequence RoPE. An explicit boolean mask allows only key positions
at or before each query's original position; short-query `mask="causal"` would
align from the right and does not express this contract.

All tensors and arithmetic remain FP32. Ten tiny CPU tests pass: a property
test compares the complete selected model/head against full upstream outputs
with H16/Q32/KV16, changing candidate counts, endpoint order, duplicates, sequence
length and padding; another verifies array-offset RoPE exactly equals gathering
from full-sequence rotation and rejects a zero-offset control. A deterministic
uniform-GQA oracle shows that lower-right short-query causal masking gives
the wrong endpoint means. Cache restoration is checked when initial clearing,
scoring or synchronization fails. Failed/incomplete quality receipts exit nonzero,
a simulated load failure preserves an explicit incomplete receipt, and a
setup failure invalidates an older passed receipt at the reused output path. These
checks establish mechanics; the separate real Metal assay below establishes
checkpoint parity and complete latency within its frozen cohort.

The conditional whole-final-block ceiling is only about 1.036×. K/V remains
13.33% of that block's configured linear work; the potentially selected Q/O/MLP
portion is 86.67%. With seven endpoints among roughly 200 tokens, eliminating
unneeded rows saves only about 3% of total configured projection work before
new reshape/mask and dispatch overhead. This limited ceiling must justify any
extra maintenance surface.

The predeclared real assay uses every frozen 77-case request, a 512 MiB inactive
allocator-cache cap for both arms, and identical FP32 weights/tokenization.
The cap is set before loading, cleared once then, and restored on exit; screen
and warmup history is recorded, with no per-arm clearing during measured pairs.
Every arm must first pass the stored CPU numerical/rank/selection/accuracy gate.
Only then run five alternating warmed complete-cohort pairs with raw scores,
repository and installed Qwen3/RoPE source snapshots taken before loading,
and untimed per-cycle allocator/process
telemetry. A candidate needs median speedup at least 1.02× and paired p05 above 1×,
followed by scalar confirmation, before even considering a production change.
The frozen CPU reference hash is captured before loading. Every completed timed
cycle is flushed to a JSONL sidecar; the main receipt remains `passed=false`,
`completed=false` until the full assay finishes. Quality failure exits nonzero
after saving the receipt. Interruption or setup failure stays incomplete.

Both bounded real processes completed successfully: B8 in 41.26 seconds and B1
in 48.85 seconds, including loading, screens, warmups and measurements. Every
screen passed, and a pure post-run audit compared every warmup and measured
cycle independently with the frozen CPU reference. Each arm/load has 462/462
equal selections and rankings, 402/462 correct decisions (67/77 per cycle), and
finite scores within the unchanged tolerances. The endpoint arm's maximum
absolute logit/probability differences are 1.335e-5/2.490e-6 at B8 and
1.454e-5/2.996e-6 at B1. These are runtime equivalence results on training-source
development requests; checkpoint exposure is unknown.

| Load | Five alternating pair speedups | Median | Sample p05 | 2% gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B8 | 1.02298, 1.02656, 1.02375, 1.02361, 1.02953 | 1.02375× | 1.02311× | Pass |
| B1 | 1.01913, 1.01929, 1.02627, 1.01619, 1.01764 | 1.01913× | 1.01648× | Fail |

The median complete-cohort latencies are 2819.98/2750.17 ms for baseline/endpoint
at B8 and 3393.38/3333.31 ms at B1. Every observed pair is faster, consistent
with the small Amdahl ceiling, but scalar confirmation falls below the declared
2% threshold. Sample percentiles from five pairs are not confidence bounds or
proof of a universal gain. Production stays on the maintained whole-block
path; the modest result does not justify adding this extra inference path now.

Raw receipts, exact source archives, incremental cycles, allocator/process
telemetry and bounded-parent status are retained as `mlx-endpoints77-b{8,1}.*`
under `benchmarks/analysis/results/`. The parent timeout reproducer is
`mlx-endpoints-bounded.executed.py`; `mlx-endpoints-reference-audit.executed.py`
and its JSON receipt preserve the independent all-cycle CPU comparison.
Numerical `passed` and `performance_gate_passed` are separate fields so a
completed negative speed result cannot be mistaken for a failed experiment.

## Combined prefix and endpoint hypothesis

The independent scalar assays show small positive gains from immutable
25-token prefix reuse (median 1.01073×) and endpoint-only final-block work
(1.01913×). Their combination has a present measured motivation, but multiplying
these speedups would not establish a combined gain. The prospective experiment
must independently pass strict full-cohort parity and median speedup at least
1.02× with sample p05 above 1× at both B8 and B1 before any production proposal.

The originally measured `combined.py` subclassed the experimental prefix scorer's
narrow readout hook. Its retained source archives preserve that version. Prefix
validation, suffix packing, original full padding, caller
order, fresh cache ownership and whole-batch fallback stay with `PrefixScorer`.
Earlier Transformer blocks use maintained cache-aware attention masks and RoPE.
The endpoint helper retains cached prefix K/V plus every suffix K/V row, rotates
suffix K at the prefix offset, rotates selected Q at each original absolute
position, and masks full keys against those absolute positions. Only the last
block's Q/O/MLP and final norm visit selected readouts. No gold enters model calls.

Thirty-five tiny CPU tests across the combined, prefix and endpoint suites pass.
The combined checks challenge H16/Q32/KV16, GQA, changing candidate counts,
lengths, padding and order, repeated/interleaved scalar and batch calls,
immutable prefix state across cache growth, mismatched/overlapping batch fallback,
duplicate readouts and incorrect absolute RoPE or causal masks. Invalid candidate
counts retain Kai's existing rejection. Four CLI checks also preserve declared
strategy selection and nonzero failure/incomplete status. These establish
mechanics separately from the real checkpoint assay. The protocol uses the same
512 MiB allocator cap for
both arms, independent all-cycle CPU gates, five alternating warmed pairs,
raw outputs, source/reference snapshots and a 180-second parent timeout per shape.

Independent source review approved the bounded assay. Both processes completed
without timeout: B8 in 39.55 seconds and B1 in 48.99 seconds. Every full-cohort
screen passed. At each load, all 924 warm/measured rows across both arms pass
the frozen CPU gate: 924 equal selections and rankings, 804 correct decisions
(67/77 per cycle), and unchanged numerical tolerances. Maximum absolute
logit/probability differences are 1.609e-5/4.615e-6 at B8 and 1.889e-5/3.936e-6
at B1. Scores are finite; neither semantic quality improvement nor held-out
quality is established.

| Load | Five alternating pair speedups | Median | Sample p05 | 2% gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B8 | 1.10287, 1.11641, 1.10561, 1.11237, 1.10707 | 1.10707× | 1.10342× | Pass |
| B1 | 1.02556, 1.02708, 1.02265, 1.02964, 1.02004 | 1.02556× | 1.02056× | Pass |

Median complete-cohort baseline/candidate latencies are 2823.69/2545.26 ms at
B8 and 3387.18/3301.63 ms at B1. Prefix preparation costs 33.00/32.55 ms, excluded
from warm/measured calls and recorded separately; the logical frozen KV state
is 5,734,400 bytes. Views can retain additional backing allocation. These gains
are independently measured rather than products of the separate assays. Sample
percentiles describe five observed pairs, not confidence bounds.

B8 peak active allocation grows from about 3.853 GB for the baseline to 4.059 GB
for the combined arm; B1 falls from about 3.025 GB to 2.896–2.902 GB. These measured
shape-dependent peaks are separate from logical prefix bytes and inactive cache.

Both loads clear the declared gate, supporting consideration of an explicit
eager immutable prefix resource. The frozen prefix includes this cohort's fixed
banking-support context; an arbitrary deployment does not necessarily share it.
Mismatch or overlapping readouts use the intact original scorer, and no automatic
25-token cache policy is supported. Independent receipt review passed. The
validated mechanics now have an explicit opt-in production scorer, with unchanged
loader/CLI defaults. The final moved-source confirmation passes both gates:
B8 median 1.11334×/p05 1.10827× and B1 median 1.02620×/p05 1.02036×, preserving
all 924 CPU-comparison rankings and selections at each load. It has separate
`mlx-prefix-production77-b{8,1}.*` receipts; the original combined receipts remain
unchanged. [Prefix usage](prefix.md) states its fixed-resource obligations and fallback
behavior.

Raw results, all-cycle CPU comparisons, incremental measured cycles, process
telemetry and exact source archives are `mlx-combined77-b{8,1}.*` in the analysis
results directory. `mlx-combined-bounded.executed.py` preserves the exact parent
reproducer and its hash appears in each `.wall.json` receipt. Historical endpoint
and prefix receipts retain their original bytes and source snapshots.

## Mixed storage probe

A tiny CPU-only MLX graph probe uses FP32 input and losslessly converts weights
whose values are representable in BF16 to FP16 storage. Its output remains FP32,
and the exported graph places an `AsType` node after the half-weight transpose
and before `Matmul`. The tiny output is exact against its FP32 control. This
does not establish a faster FP16-input/FP32-accumulation Metal kernel: graph
conversion and potential temporary storage need investigation before a speed
claim. It also does not establish full-checkpoint quality. The retained probe,
graph and receipt are `mlx-mixed-storage.executed.py`, `.dot` and `.json` under
the analysis results directory.

## Allocator cache hypothesis

MLX distinguishes active buffers from inactive buffers retained for reuse.
`get_cache_memory()` measures the latter, while peak memory measures active
buffers. Active plus cached memory therefore matters when studying process
footprint. A cache limit controls allocator reuse; it is separate from an
application's prompt KV cache. [MLX cache API](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/python/_autosummary/mlx.core.set_cache_limit.html)

The pinned 0.32.3 Metal allocator initializes both its memory guideline and
cache cap to `min(1.5*recommended_working_set, 0.95*physical_memory)`, nominally
24.481 GB on this Mac. Its reclamation threshold is
`min(0.95*recommended_working_set, memory_guideline)`, nominally 18.116 GB.
Allocation tries buffer reuse first; a cache miss can trigger reclamation.
The cap is then enforced, while freeing one buffer can temporarily overshoot it.
These are source mechanics, not evidence that retained cache caused the historical
latency outliers. [Pinned allocator source](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.32.3/mlx/backend/metal/allocator.cpp#L54-L61)

Installed MLX-LM 0.31.3 periodically clears allocator cache during generation and
after evaluation prefill chunks; its server/generator separately manages wired
memory. The installed source has no `set_cache_limit` calls. A bounded inactive
cache could reduce footprint or stability variation without changing math, but
the fresh comparison must record synchronized active/cache/peak snapshots per
cycle and process/system diagnostics outside timed work. Neither a changed
default nor a causal explanation for old outliers is currently supported.
`set_cache_limit` returns the previous cap; there is no corresponding cache-cap
getter in the installed Python API. A fresh experimental process must record
and restore that setting if changed.

## Reproduction and provenance

Run Metal commands with the project's approved GPU permissions. A Torch-free
editable `wyat[mlx]` environment was used at `/tmp/wyat-mlx-only`:

```sh
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" /tmp/wyat-mlx-only/bin/python benchmarks/analysis/mlx/profile.py
PYTHONPATH="$PWD" /tmp/wyat-mlx-only/bin/python benchmarks/analysis/mlx/fusion.py
```

The original profile receipt is preserved byte-for-byte; exact original runner
bytes were not archived and remain unknown. Its provenance sidecar
hashes the receipt and retained reproducer/backend sources and explicitly records
that source hashes were added afterward: trace-only and case-limit runner
branches were introduced after the original timed profile. Fresh runner outputs
include source hashes directly. Synchronization is explicit stage fences for
diagnostics, and output evaluation plus host materialization for normal scoring.

files.text:
# Padding and ready-cohort scheduling

This experiment uses the same pinned Kai weights and 77 training-source requests
as the [stage profile](mlx.md). Labels are outside scoring, and model exposure to
these examples is unknown. All comparisons retain FP32 weights/activations,
original candidate order, endpoint positions, and the existing strict quality
gates. No production packing or scheduling policy changes.

The [runner](../../benchmarks/analysis/mlx/padding.py) compares ordinary
pad-to-eight caller-order microbatches with exact widths, stable length grouping,
and both together. Microbatch size is eight. Grouping includes an additional
encoding pass to obtain actual lengths; its cost is inside timing. Results are
restored to caller order, including duplicate requests. Hypothesis tests use an
independent scheduler oracle to challenge that restoration.

Length grouping reduces padded projection tokens from 14,840 to 14,072 on this
cohort: an arithmetic work ratio of 1.0546. Dense attention work has ratio 1.1107.
These are work estimates, not timing predictions. Removing padding can change
kernel shapes, tile utilization, compilation, and allocator reuse.

Each arm passed the CPU-reference screen, then five alternating warmed complete
cohort pairs. All 385 repeated selections and full rankings matched its control;
each cycle retained 67/77 independently labeled-correct predictions. Raw logits,
probabilities, timings and failures are in the [immutable receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-padding77-b8.json).
Its runner hash matches the [executed source snapshot](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-padding77-b8.executed.txt).

| Arm | Median baseline/candidate speed | Paired p05–p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Exact width | 1.0365× | 0.8489–1.0494× |
| Length grouping | 1.0534× | 0.7540–1.3098× |
| Grouping plus exact width | 0.9665× | 0.8217–1.0435× |

The individual timings are unstable, and the combined candidate is slower at
the median. These observations do not support a production speedup claim or
policy change. Paired percentiles describe the five observed ratios; they are
not confidence intervals. The profiler and earlier scaling assay also contain
material timing variation, prompting a separate allocator-cache hypothesis.

Outer benchmark calls contain all 77 ready requests. Their row residence metric
is complete-cohort call residence, rather than internal microbatch residence or
online admission/queue latency. Loading, warmups and output serialization are
outside timed cycles. Host logits are materialized before the scorer returns.
Per-cycle allocator/cache and fault telemetry was not collected in this assay;
the later [system observation](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/system-conditions.json)
cannot establish the cause of its earlier delays.

files.name: docs/analysis/plan.md
files.text:
# Kai engine optimization protocol

The target is complete, synchronous decision inference on the pinned Kai model,
not a decoder benchmark. The baseline is current FP32 MLX eager inference,
with unchanged choice rendering, candidate order and relative-softmax semantics.
CPU and CUDA observations are separate runtime baselines. No 20x target is
claimed achieved merely by switching hardware.

Use the existing 77-case BANKING77 training-source development cohort, preserved
raw predictions and model identity. Its six-choice menus are a runtime assay;
prior model exposure is unknown. Reserved confirmation stays closed.

## Decomposition and decision rules

Measure request validation/serialization/tokenization, batch packing, embeddings,
28 attention/MLP blocks, final normalization/gather, candidate head, host
materialization and decision interpretation. Loading is measured separately.
Synchronizing intermediate stages changes execution/fusion: stage sums must be
compared with ordinary whole inference, with diagnostic overhead reported.

Amdahl's law bounds a proposed stage improvement:

    whole speedup = 1 / ((1 - fraction) + fraction / stage_speedup)

Even eliminating a 5% stage caps whole speedup at 1.053x. Eliminating one of 28
uniform-cost layers caps it at 1.037x; uniform cost is an assumption to test.
Optimize dominant measured work before introducing state or specialized kernels.
A 20x whole-engine gain from one stage requires that stage to exceed 95% of
ordinary cost at finite acceleration; exactly 95% permits 20x only if its cost
vanishes. A conditional device-work fraction cannot establish that ordinary
whole-engine fraction.

Roofline diagnostics use explicit shapes and conservative FLOP/byte counts.
Effective rates are measurements; a hardware peak is not invented. Count
padding work and memory traffic separately from useful request work. A lower
bound on bytes is not a measurement of actual device bandwidth.

The user's [Universal Scaling Law collection](https://teilo.xyz/collections/universal-scaling-law/)
and [Gunther's primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1431) inform repeated
six-level sweeps. Retain raw throughput, residuals and invalid/weak fits. Batch
size changes work granularity and padding, so fitted coefficients cannot by
themselves establish cache coherence or processor contention. CPU thread counts
also span heterogeneous performance/efficiency cores on this M4 Pro.

Little's law applies only to a stated steady-state admission/queue system;
offline ready-batch residence times cannot establish online queue latency.

## Candidate queue

These are hypotheses, not promised wins. Profiling and scaling order the queue.

| Candidate | Falsifier or acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Length grouping or exact padding widths | Reduced padded work and whole-cohort latency; original output order and all quality gates preserved |
| Fused QKV and gate/up projections | Fewer dispatches or better GEMM utilization; no duplicate retained weights or whole-latency regression |
| Lossless narrow weight storage with FP32 computation | Exact stored values, observed kernel dtype/traffic, numerical parity and a measured complete gain |
| Selective precision instead of whole-backbone casts | Independently declared strict gates pass on all 77 cases; no tolerance relaxation after results |
| Endpoint-only final block work | Causal equivalence, actual last-block fraction and enough gain to justify maintenance |
| Shared-prefix prefill | Identical tokens/positions/readouts, explicit cache ownership and resource limits, benefit at measured prefix reuse |
| Maintained vLLM/SGLang mechanisms | Actual candidate endpoint/head contract support; installation/device cost justified by measured benefit |
| Targeted Metal kernels | A dominant primitive is identified; standard kernel oracle and whole-model quality/latency both pass |

Before production edits, retain at least five alternating warmed comparison
pairs with the same artifact and input hash. Every selection and full ranking
must agree, no labeled-accuracy loss or failures are allowed, logits use the
existing 1e-3 absolute/relative gate and probability differences stay <=1e-4.
Failures and rejected ideas remain in receipts. Small numerical fixtures and
Hypothesis challenge connected boundaries; independent review verifies the
result and scope. Typed functions and short role-based files remain required.

Full Xcode/Metal System Trace is available when run with its required cache/device
access. Initial RTX 4070 Ti probes found active compute; no workload was run
against it. A later idle observation opened the separately declared
[CUDA numerical control](cuda-run.md), with asset admission, per-batch ownership
checks and owned process caps. An idle snapshot does not reserve the device.

## Observed decisions

The [stage profile](mlx.md) attributes about 49.7% of fenced stage time to MLPs
and 40.1% to attention. Fencing adds 18.2% diagnostic overhead, so these are
conditional fractions, not ordinary request-latency measurements. Eliminating
the entire final block would cap the conditional gain near 1.036x. The prepared
endpoint experiment tested whether its smaller saving survived dispatch overhead.
An independent read of the frozen token vectors found a common 25-token prefix
across all 77 cases: 1,925 of 13,679 token rows, or 14.07%. This is a configured
linear-work opportunity, not a latency saving. Maintained prefix-cache reuse is
tested with maintained masks, RoPE offsets and fresh per-call state ownership.
The [storage audit](storage.md) separately found no maintained mixed
FP32-activation/BF16-weight direct-load path; halved weight storage alone does
not establish halved DRAM traffic or faster inference.

| Completed assay | Evidence and decision |
| --- | --- |
| [Six CPU thread budgets](cpu.md) | Eight best among sampled counts; all 3,234 outputs pass. Descriptive USL peak near ten predicts only 0.3% over fitted eight, below residuals and observed variation. Keep eight. |
| [CPU operator profile](cpu.md) | All 28 layers already dispatch CPU flash GQA. GEMMs account for about 75.7% of profiled self time; attention accounts for 8.61%. These diagnostic fractions prioritize matrix work without establishing ordinary latency fractions. |
| [CPU FP32 gate/up packing](cpu.md) | Strict quality gates pass at both shapes. Batch-eight median 1.02047x passes locally; scalar 1.01494x misses the original 1.02 threshold. Reject production promotion after two-shape confirmation. |
| [Frozen CPU projection max-autotune](cpu.md) | Exact local projection outputs; ATen mm selected over the slower CPP candidate. Warm paired median 0.98404x, not an improvement. No full-model compile proposal. |
| [CPU exact prefix reuse](cpu.md) | Earlier experimental snapshot: native M4 Pro full77 medians 1.10097x at batch eight and 1.07610x scalar. All 2,156 outputs and four prospectively declared CPU performance gates pass; independent audit agrees. Cold prefix build about 68–69 ms, per-call copying included. Subsequent resource selection retained this ownership; final-source production confirmation follows below. |
| [One-use CPU cache resource screen](cpu.md) | Three fresh native process pairs reduce sampled inference-body RSS by 421–428 MB (9.53–9.67%), passing the frozen resource thresholds. All 288 outputs on eight unique cases and masked flash GQA pass. Selected K/V storage 358.06→62.55 MB; intrusive observer cost 1.48–1.54x. Full77/scalar selection results follow below; no CPU production or speed claim. |
| [One-use CPU full77 latency](cpu.md) | All 3,696 strict outputs pass. Relative to retained prefix, medians 0.99979x/1.00143x fail selection at batch eight/scalar (p05 fails both); reject one-use ownership. Relative to full prefill, 1.10928x/1.07313x pass original gates. Sampled memory gain does not override the latency rejection; production unchanged. |
| [Final opt-in CPU prefix scorer](cpu/prefix.md) | Final-source medians 1.10038x at B8 and 1.07260x at B1; all four original performance gates pass at both shapes. Independent audits preserve all 2,204 strict outcomes; one B1 pair regresses to 0.99801x and remains recorded. Explicit retained prefix, full final block and whole-batch fallback; default loading unchanged. Connected native CPU/Metal/DMBench regression passes 971 tests. |
| [CPU selected final readouts](cpu/readout/confirm.md) | Independent scalar full77 audit preserves all 1,078 strict outcomes and 67/77 correct per cohort. Retained-relative median 1.00853x and p05 0.98916x fail the original selection gates; two of five pairs regress. Reject promotion and skip B8 confirmation. Production keeps the complete final block; scalar timing is unprofiled. |
| [Native current CPU versus MLX](runtime/native.md) | All 924 measured/warmup outcomes preserve gold-reference and cross-backend numerical gates, full ranks and 67/77 correct per cohort. Full-stock MLX GPU versus eight-thread full-stock Torch CPU passes four original performance gates: median 2.83972x, p05 2.79313x, aggregate 2.82992x, p95 ratio 0.349892. Existing explicit backend selection is supported on this host/artifact; this is not an increment over prior MLX or a server/held-out claim. |
| [CPU packed projection primitive](cpu/projection.md) | All 96 calls on four authentic layer-zero operands preserve exact FP32 output hashes. KV medians 1.01678–1.04164x and QKV medians 1.03274–1.07154x miss the predeclared 1.12x triage filter; scalar-192 KV and B8 QKV tails regress. Both variants ineligible for this follow-up screen; no full-model candidate or promotion. Initial supervisor-sidecar failure and corrected auditor singleton-stride assumption remain preserved separately. |
| [Six MLX batch sizes](scaling.md) | All strict gates pass; aggregate USL parameters are invalid. Preserve the stalls and reject a physical optimum claim. |
| [Packed QKV/gate-up](mlx.md) | All rankings pass; paired medians 0.984x, 0.996x and 0.976x. Retain maintained projections. |
| [Exact padding/length grouping](padding.md) | Smaller estimated padded work; paired variation crosses regressions. No production promotion. |
| [512 MiB inactive cache cap](cache.md) | Batch-eight retained active-plus-cache allocation 9.32 to 2.93 GB, roughly 0.7% throughput cost. Expose an explicit process-owned CLI option; default policy unchanged. |
| [Endpoint-only final block](mlx.md) | Batch-eight median 1.024x, scalar 1.019x; strict parity throughout. Scalar misses the declared 1.02 threshold, so keep experimental. |
| [Exact prefix reuse](prefix.md) | Batch-eight median 1.078x, scalar 1.011x; strict parity throughout. Batch-eight peak active memory rises about 206 MB. Scalar misses the same promotion threshold. |
| [Combined prefix and endpoint](mlx.md) | Independently measured batch-eight median 1.107x and scalar 1.026x; all five pairs faster at both shapes, with strict parity. Both original gates pass on this fixed-prefix cohort. |
| [Final opt-in production prefix](prefix.md) | Moved-source confirmation measured 1.113x batch-eight and 1.026x scalar; both original gates pass. Default loading stays on full prefill, with eager explicit prefix construction and whole-batch fallback. |
| [Selective MLP FP16 storage eligibility](precision.md) | All 84 selected tensors fail exact round-trip storage: 43,137 changed values, including 224 rounded to zero. All six declared arms rejected before model allocation or inference; keep FP32 production. |
| [Maintained BF16 MLP products](bfloat.md) | All three fixed role arms fail strict numerical gates at batch eight and scalar despite exact parameters, finite predictions and unchanged top choices. Full ranks and logit/probability drift reject every arm; no timing or production change. |
| [Direct BF16 loads with FP32 projection arithmetic](mixed.md) | One real gate projection preserves exact cold outputs and all 744 output hashes; independent FP64 checks pass. The fixed 32×32 tile is slower at all four shapes (prefix medians 0.546x scalar, 0.401x batch eight). Reject promotion. The [tile work account](mixed-tile.md) supports a separately frozen 64×64 reuse test, without predicting success. |
| [64×64 output reuse](tile.md) | Exact previously captured activations/weights and all cold/warm/timed hashes pass. Maintained/new64 prefix medians 0.18167x scalar and 0.14830x batch eight fail unchanged gates; frozen32/new64 medians 0.37292x/0.36384x also show regression. Reject promotion. Logical read reduction did not translate to speed; register/occupancy/shared-memory causes remain unknown. |
| [Explicit fragment-loop unrolling](unroll.md) | All 748 outputs preserve exact maintained FP32 bits. Prefix medians improve 1.927x/1.995x over frozen64, but maintained/unrolled medians 0.35280x/0.29556x fail unchanged gates. Both full controls fail; reject promotion. No spill diagnosis or whole-engine gain follows. |
| [Ready Metal capture and bounded replay](trace.md) | Two dispatch captures preserve cold bits and raw inventories. Offline compiler unavailable; one 120-second headless replay yielded no profiling fields. Client killed/reaped; hidden XPC state unknown. Register/occupancy hypotheses remain unmeasured. |
| [CUDA FP32 numerical control](cuda-run.md) | Batch one passes all 77 strict CPU-reference selections/ranks/logit/probability gates with 67 correct and no failures. Observed FP32/autocast-off dtypes and forced math SDPA; independent raw audit verifies assets, source and terminal cleanup. Peak reserved memory 2.441 GB. Cold observer-instrumented cohort supports no speed or promotion claim. |
| [CUDA batch geometry and released precision](cuda-run.md) | Batch-eight FP32 passes all 77 strict gates against CPU and CUDA batch one; peak reserved memory 2.691 GB. Released BF16 batch one retains all top choices but changes five full ranks, with maximum probability drift 0.015278 against CPU; reject under unchanged gates. All owned workers exit and GPU returns to idle. No warmed speed comparison or default change. |
| [CUDA FP32 efficient-attention screen](attention.md) | Corrected B1/B8 diagnostics pass all 50 outcomes on eight unique cases under unchanged numerical/ranking gates, with 28 actual FP32 CUTLASS attention kernels per candidate profile. Independent raw audits agree. Original observer failure remains archived. These screen receipts establish no full77 parity or warmed speed; the following full-cohort study supplies that separate evidence. |
| [CUDA full77 and paired body latency](latency-results.md) | Independent audits preserve all 2,482 outcomes and strict gates. Six warmed pairs support median 1.0565x at B1 and 1.0653x at B8 against FP32 math attention. B1 repeated-row residence p95 regresses 1.65%, concentrated in the four longest cases. Representative MLP costs nominate packed gate/up; exact kernel-grid tail diagnostics remain pending. No online, 20x, held-out-quality or production-promotion claim. |
| [CUDA projection storage preparation](cuda/packing.md) | A local CPU probe on real layer-zero weights and cached activations preserves exact outputs and one shared 24 MiB gate/up backing; nine tests including Hypothesis pass. Full-model/CUDA parity, device aliases, peak memory and speed remain unmeasured. The reviewed native L192/L197 diagnostic awaits changed-payload transfer authorization. |
| [Server admission under pool saturation](server/admission.md) | Reproduced concurrent requests returning 200 instead of documented 503 when the shared pool has one token. Admission now precedes pool dispatch, with atomic queued/worker cancellation ownership. Five focused tests including 12 Hypothesis histories and full 894-test native/DMBench regression pass. Model arithmetic is unchanged; no HTTP throughput or latency claim. |

These assays use one pinned release and 77 unique training-source development
cases. Repeated predictions establish numerical/runtime behavior within this
assay, not new independent quality evidence. Raw failures, repeats, telemetry
and declared source archives remain beside each receipt. Native DMBench role
projection is separately [contract-tested](../dmbench-integration.md); the old
full-model pilot used the original verbatim recipe. A separately frozen native
development assay now retains all 30 cases: six expected 2,048-token admission
failures and 24 admitted authored cases, with matching scalar/batch selections.
The released artifact allows 255 choices; the 64-choice limit in the fixture
was deliberately configured for a boundary test. No menu was reduced.

The endpoint and prefix gains were measured separately and must not be
multiplied or added. The subsequent combined assay measured its own complete
latency and passed full quality and five-pair gates at both batch eight and
scalar. Independent inspection verified all cycles, source archives and original
thresholds. These results motivate one explicitly configured, eagerly built
prefix scorer; they do not establish a universal default or online queue gain.

# Selective projection precision: prospective protocol

The current MLX control remains eager full-prefill FP32 with the pinned Kai
weights, segmented tokenizer and candidate head. Whole-backbone BF16 and FP16
previously failed strict output gates. This experiment asks whether limiting
reduced precision to particular MLP projection roles avoids that failure.
No production precision policy changes.

## Eligibility before inference

All 196 serialized projection tensors are BF16. BF16's significand precision
fits FP16's, but its exponent range and subnormal grid do not. For every selected
tensor, first measure finite FP32 → FP16 → FP32 equality on its actual values.
Retain names, shapes, element counts, changed values, maximum errors and
overflow/underflow observations. Derive arm eligibility from its actual MLP
projection set; unrelated attention tensors cannot reject an MLP arm.

A failed exact-storage guard rejects that declared arm before inference. It
does not justify silently relabeling lossy weights as lossless or loosening the
guard. An approximation with changed weights would need a separate prospective
contract. This check can decisively reject the family without loading a model.

## Fixed arm family

| Arm | Selected MLP products |
| --- | --- |
| All down | Down projection in all 28 layers |
| All gate/up | Gate and up projections in all 28 layers |
| All MLP | All three projections in all 28 layers |
| First four | All three projections in layers 0–3 |
| Last four | All three projections in layers 24–27 |
| Last one | All three projections in layer 27; diagnostic only |

For an eligible arm, selected products use maintained FP16 inputs and weights
and restore outputs to FP32. SwiGLU, embeddings, attention, norms, residuals and
the head stay FP32. Input and output rounding remain intentional numerical
changes even with exact stored weights; FP32 accumulation cannot undo them.
The single-layer Amdahl ceiling assumes uniform costs and fenced fractions,
so diagnostic status is a declared budget decision, not a proof of impossibility.

## Evidence and acceptance

Set `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0` before framework import. Freeze source, parameter and
input identities. Keep the same 512 MiB allocator cap and token-cache-zero
conditions. Screen every eligible arm on all 77 frozen training-source cases at
batch eight and scalar. Preserve every selection and full ranking, no failures
or labeled-accuracy loss, the existing 1e-3 absolute/relative logit rule, and
maximum probability drift 1e-4. Retain failed and ineligible arms.

Only numerical survivors can enter five alternating warmed timing pairs.
Production consideration requires median speedup at least 1.02 and paired
sample p05 above one at both shapes, plus a challenge on the frozen longer,
variable-menu native DMBench cases. These development screens do not establish
held-out quality. Separate bounded parent processes retain timeout/failure
receipts. A changed projection recipe requires freshly built prefix state;
existing FP32 prefixes must never be reused across changed arithmetic.

## Observed eligibility result

The bounded CPU-only scan completed in 2.122 seconds; its parent exited in
2.228 seconds without timeout. All 84 selected MLP tensors failed exact FP16
storage eligibility. Across 264,241,152 elements, 43,137 values changed and 224
rounded to zero. No source nonfinite values, FP16 overflows or BF16-source
subnormals were found. The largest finite absolute change was
`2.9802322387695312e-8`. These failures arise in the FP16 subnormal grid despite
finite, normal BF16 source values. Small absolute errors do not waive the
prospective exact-storage contract.

| Declared arm | Selected elements | Ineligible selected tensors | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| All down | 88,080,384 | 28 / 28 | Rejected before inference |
| All gate/up | 176,160,768 | 56 / 56 | Rejected before inference |
| All MLP | 264,241,152 | 84 / 84 | Rejected before inference |
| First four | 37,748,736 | 12 / 12 | Rejected before inference |
| Last four | 37,748,736 | 12 / 12 | Rejected before inference |
| Last one, diagnostic | 9,437,184 | 3 / 3 | Rejected before inference |

The [raw receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-mlp-fp16-eligibility.json)
retains every tensor and mechanically derived arm outcome. The
[parent receipt](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-mlp-fp16-eligibility.wall.json)
records exit 1 as a completed negative eligibility result, distinct from an
incomplete error or timeout. Checkpoint SHA256 before and after scanning is
`43369a2bfddb61495beb7cea6bf30d7564a5c5caff31f4dbf2e6cfce48423b69`;
the validated pinned Kai identity also matches prior assays. No Torch or MLX
was imported, no model was allocated, and no inference or speed measurement
was performed. The fixed guard rejects all six arms; production is unchanged.

The [scanner](../../benchmarks/analysis/mlx/eligibility.py) reads exact BF16
values in bounded 262,144-element CPU chunks, validates selected shapes and
disjoint byte spans, writes partial receipts after each tensor and bounds its
owned child to 120 seconds. Existing receipts are not overwritten. Fourteen
tiny/property tests passed, including an independent Python half conversion
oracle, BF16/FP16 exponent and subnormal counterexamples, malformed spans,
per-arm role/layer intersections and failure/timeout retention. Independent
source and tiny-test review preceded the real scan.

Both prospective declarations remain archived: the original scanner declaration
and source bytes in
[the executed source archive](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-mlp-fp16-eligibility.sources-960d68e2ea757b13.json),
and this document's original protocol identity in
[the protocol sidecar](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-mlp-fp16-eligibility.protocol.json).
The live protocol and results now have this single owner. Eligibility evidence
is limited to the pinned checkpoint's selected parameter values; it establishes
neither model quality nor a claim about other checkpoints.

files.text:
# Explicit native MLX prefix reuse

`PrefixScorer` prepares one exact immutable token prefix eagerly for a loaded Kai
model. Matching requests reuse its fixed K/V state and evaluate the final
Transformer block only at the candidate/query readouts. It implements the normal
Wyat scorer contract, so `Model` and `create_app` need no separate integration.
Existing loading and CLI defaults retain full prefill.
The full server example requires the `mlx` and `server` extras; from this
checkout, install them with `uv pip install -e '.[mlx,server]'`.

```python
from wyat import Candidate, Model, Request
from wyat.backends.kai.mlx import MLXKaiScorer
from wyat.backends.kai.prefix import PrefixScorer
from wyat.server import create_app

base = MLXKaiScorer.from_directory("/models/kai", device="gpu", compile=False)
example = Request(
    context="Classify customer banking support requests into the supplied intents.",
    query="I have a missing refund",
    candidates=(Candidate("refund", "Missing refund"), Candidate("card", "Card problem")),
)
exact_prefix = base.encode_request(example).ids[:25]
scorer = PrefixScorer(base, exact_prefix)
model = Model(scorer, scorer.model_id)
decision = model.decide(example)
app = create_app(model)
```

The prefix length here is an explicit application choice, not an automatic
25-token policy. Choose token IDs shared by the intended requests, produced by
this model's exact encoding recipe. A text prefix alone does not establish the
same token prefix. The constructor requires an exact tuple of valid integer IDs,
nonempty and shorter than the encoder's maximum length. Compiled bases and
scaled RoPE are rejected before cache construction; this path has evidence only
for eager inference with the released unscaled Kai contract.

The per-batch array-offset RoPE API is present in the declared minimum
[MLX 0.30.0 source](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/v0.30.0/python/src/fast.cpp),
and [MLX-LM 0.30.0](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/v0.30.0/mlx_lm/models/rope_utils.py)
selects that native RoPE implementation for the unscaled model. This source check
establishes API presence, not older-version numerical or performance results.
The recorded measurements used MLX 0.32.3 and MLX-LM 0.31.3.

Keep the base weights, decision head, device and encoder fixed for the resource's
lifetime. Create a new resource after replacing any of them. The `prefix` and
base `compiled` properties are read-only. Preparation finishes before the
constructor returns; its cost belongs to setup. `prefix_state_bytes` reports
logical K/V bytes, while views may retain additional backing allocation. The
scorer never changes the process-wide MLX allocator limits.

Each admitted batch gets fresh cache owners from the immutable prefix snapshots.
Every suffix token remains in K/V, with original RoPE positions and an explicit
absolute causal mask for selected final queries. Candidate/query positions are
translated once; full right padding and caller/candidate order are preserved.
If any request differs from the exact prefix or has a readout inside it, the
whole batch uses the original base scorer. Admission encoding and fallback
encoding both count toward that call's work. No suffix state survives between
requests. `create_app` continues to serialize active inference for the shared
model and encoder.

The independently audited experimental combined path preserved the frozen CPU
rankings, selections and numerical tolerances on all 77 development requests.
Five alternating pairs measured median speedups of 1.10707× at B8 and 1.02556×
at B1, clearing the declared 2% gate at both loads. Preparation took about 33 ms
and retained 5,734,400 logical K/V bytes. The prefix contains that cohort's fixed
banking context; these measurements establish neither a universal gain nor
held-out model quality. B8 peak active allocation grew from about 3.853 to
4.059 GB; B1 peak active allocation fell from about 3.025 to 2.90 GB. Peak active
allocation is distinct from logical prefix size and cached inactive allocation.
Raw provenance and limits are in [the MLX analysis](mlx.md). Final production
source confirmation is recorded separately from these original experimental
receipts.

The final production source passed a fresh full-cohort confirmation at both
loads, with the same 512 MiB allocator cap, strict CPU numerical/rank/selection
gate and five alternating warmed pairs. Each load preserved all 924 compared
warm/measured rankings and selections, with accuracy unchanged at 67/77 per
cycle. Maximum absolute logit/probability differences were 1.609e-5/4.615e-6
at B8 and 1.889e-5/3.936e-6 at B1.

| Load | Median paired speedup | Sample p05 | Baseline/cached cohort p50 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B8 | 1.11334× | 1.10827× | 2834.87/2546.27 ms |
| B1 | 1.02620× | 1.02036× | 3383.95/3301.33 ms |

Both clear the original median >=1.02× and sample p05 >1× gate. B1 retains an
observed pair of 1.01973×; the gate uses the declared median and percentile,
and does not require every pair to exceed 2%. Preparation cost 32.63/33.57 ms
at B8/B1 is separate from timed calls. Final useful throughput was
27.166/30.321 requests/s for baseline/cached B8 and 22.758/23.330 at B1.
The same shape-dependent peak active allocation tradeoff remained: about
3.853/4.059 GB at B8 and 3.025/2.900 GB at B1. These are workload-specific
observations, not a guarantee for another prefix, model or workload.

The new receipts are `benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-prefix-production77-b8.json`
and `mlx-prefix-production77-b1.json`, with exact source archives, ten-cycle
journals and parent `.wall.json` receipts. Both parent/child pairs exited zero
without their 180-second timeout; the Mac resources were released afterward.
The original `mlx-combined77-*` observations and archives remain unchanged.
Sample percentiles from five pairs are descriptive, not confidence bounds.

# Native CPU and MLX inference

On the current Apple Silicon host, the existing full-stock MLX backend is a
supported option for this local FP32 Kai artifact. Select it explicitly; default
loading remains Torch on CPU. No production code changed for this comparison.

## Use the measured configuration

Install the existing MLX/server extras, then keep `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0` in the
process environment before importing MLX. The 512 MiB setting controls inactive
Metal allocator buffers, not total model memory or a hard RAM bound.

```sh
uv sync --extra mlx --extra server
MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 uv run wyat serve /path/to/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --backend mlx --device gpu --max-length 512 --token-cache-size 0 \
  --mlx-cache-limit-mib 512 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
```

For library callers, launch Python with `MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0`, configure the
process-owned allocator explicitly, and load once for repeated requests:

```python
import mlx.core as mx
import wyat

mx.set_cache_limit(512 * (1 << 20))
model = wyat.load(
    "/path/to/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B",
    backend="mlx",
    device="gpu",
    max_length=512,
    token_cache_size=0,
)
# model.decide(request) or model.decide_many(requests)
```

Both tested runtime backbones and heads execute FP32. The released backbone
contains mixed BF16/F32 source tensors, expanded to FP32 at load. These settings
do not establish another artifact's numerical quality. Keep
compilation disabled for this configuration. The ordinary path performs full
prefill; the experimental selected-last-block path is not promoted.

## Reproduce the comparison

The comparison also needs the existing inference extra for its Torch baseline.
Use the canonical local 77-case JSONL file and retain stdout plus diagnostics:

```sh
uv sync --extra inference --extra mlx --extra server
MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 uv run wyat benchmark .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --backend mlx --device gpu --baseline-backend torch --baseline-device cpu \
  --batch-size 1 --baseline-batch-size 1 --max-length 512 \
  --token-cache-size 0 --torch-threads 8 --repeats 5 --warmup 1 \
  --mlx-cache-limit-mib 512 \
  < benchmarks/real/banking77-train-dev-menu6.jsonl \
  > /tmp/wyat-native-comparison.json 2> /tmp/wyat-native-comparison.log
```

The CLI exit status reports paired quality, not performance acceptance. An
external assay must also require paired median at least **1.02x**, sample p05
strictly above **1x**, aggregate cohort speedup above **1x**, and candidate cohort
p95 no worse than baseline. These four conditions are unchanged. For bounded
runs, use an owned process-group supervisor as retained in the executed source
archive; this shell example itself does not impose a wall cap.

## Observed current result

The independently audited run retained **924 outcomes**, including both warmup
cohorts and five paired measured cohorts. Every cohort has the same 77 ordered
cases and **67 correct**; no outcome failed or disappeared. All gold-reference
and cross-backend full ranks, choices, logit absolute/relative `1e-3` and
probability absolute `1e-4` gates pass. The measured paired maximum drift was
`1.54972e-5` logits and `3.04443e-6` probabilities.

| Original performance condition | Observed | Verdict |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Paired median ≥ 1.02x | 2.83972x | Pass |
| Paired sample p05 > 1x | 2.79313x | Pass |
| Aggregate cohort speedup > 1x | 2.82992x | Pass |
| Candidate/baseline cohort p95 ≤ 1 | 0.349892 | Pass |

All five paired ratios remain visible: `2.843463`, `2.839722`, `2.878087`,
`2.795916`, `2.792436`. Median complete-cohort latency was **10,009.36 ms** for
Torch CPU and **3,527.95 ms** for MLX GPU. The native inference child exited zero,
was reaped after **87.682 s** within its 180-second cap, and passed source/asset
integrity checks. The independent standard-library audit exited zero and was
reaped after **0.609 s** within its separate 60-second cap.

Observed context: macOS 27.2 arm64, Python 3.12.11, Torch 2.14.1,
Transformers 5.18.0, MLX 0.32.3 and MLX-LM 0.31.3. The executed archive contains
28 source texts, including all 22 unchanged production Python files and the
actual supervisor; eleven model/input assets were pinned before and after.

Read the [raw report](../../../benchmarks/real/runtime-cpu-mlx77-current.json),
[independent audit](../../../benchmarks/real/runtime-cpu-mlx77-current-review.json)
and [audit execution receipt](../../../benchmarks/real/runtime-cpu-mlx77-current-review.execution.json).
The raw report SHA is
`829621d533b6a7998b3c584c7533193e0e7ec09c49a4751b7fc10381c0839d65`;
the executed source archive SHA is
`1cffd68e316c10ed7e87aedb106bbef0c4c23d9eef9573d2b11d2402d92f93aa`.

The result supports this backend choice on this host, artifact and development
cohort. The exact Apple chip model was not captured. Torch uses each scalar's
logical token width; MLX rounds physical width to eight tokens, so logical
requests match while execution shapes differ. Timed dispatch was unprofiled;
`MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0` is an observed environment setting, not proof about every
kernel's internal arithmetic. Token/reference identities do not establish
independent retokenization or native binary identity. Loading, HTTP, admission
queues and JSON serialization are excluded; cumulative RSS spans both engines.
Five pairs and their interpolated p05 are not confidence bounds. These training-
source development cases do not establish held-out generalization, another
model's quality, server throughput, or a universal backend advantage.

files.text:
# Runtime mechanisms for Kai prefill

Read-only investigation, 2026-10-05. The target is one causal Qwen3 prefill,
followed by the released candidate head over ordered option endpoints and the
final query endpoint. There is no autoregressive decoding. Wyat's future trained
model shape remains open; these findings apply to the currently supported Kai
adapter.

## Evidence and source pins

These are inspected current upstream snapshots, not the versions deployed by
every user. Wyat's measured environment uses MLX 0.32.3 and MLX-LM 0.31.3.

| Repository | Inspected commit | Relevant implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| vLLM | `138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387` | [Qwen3](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3.py), [Qwen2 MLP](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen2.py) |
| SGLang | `b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e` | [Qwen3](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3.py), [Qwen2 MLP](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py) |
| MLX | `f8aaf49d4a7e4c0ccd31986b45b69d791f925ed8` | [maintained kernel/runtime source](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/tree/f8aaf49d4a7e4c0ccd31986b45b69d791f925ed8), [SDPA API](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/python/_autosummary/mlx.core.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention.html) |
| MLX-LM | `5cfec4cb39deba54210b3ff4d86f2337c7bc10b5` | [Qwen3](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/5cfec4cb39deba54210b3ff4d86f2337c7bc10b5/mlx_lm/models/qwen3.py), [compiled activation](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/5cfec4cb39deba54210b3ff4d86f2337c7bc10b5/mlx_lm/models/activations.py), [attention wrapper](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/5cfec4cb39deba54210b3ff4d86f2337c7bc10b5/mlx_lm/models/base.py) |
| vLLM Metal plugin | `2fd759dbd1171a77f7889d04a3b6d75c78fbeea3` | [pooling scope](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-metal/blob/2fd759dbd1171a77f7889d04a3b6d75c78fbeea3/docs/text_embedding_pooling.md) |

Semantic Router provenance and exact input/head semantics are recorded in
[the source investigation](../semantic-router-inference.md). In particular,
segmented tokenization, causal option ordering, original RoPE positions, head
FP32 arithmetic, calibration and rejection of overlength inputs are contracts.
Similar-looking prompts, independent candidate embeddings and normalized
sentence embeddings do not satisfy them.

Observed local baseline: [five paired full-cohort cycles](../../benchmarks/real/runtime-cpu-mlx77.json)
gave FP32 MLX Metal versus Torch CPU/8 threads a median `2.024×` speedup
(paired 5th–95th percentiles `1.850×–2.158×`). All 385 repeated selections and
rankings agreed. Maximum logit/probability differences were `1.287e-5`/
`2.462e-6`. Timing includes tokenization, batching, host results and decision
interpretation; it excludes loading, HTTP and admission queues. This is a
77-case development assay with unknown training exposure, not a quality
generalization result. [Compilation](../../benchmarks/real/mlx-fp32-compile77.json)
was `0.990×`; full BF16 and FP16 failed the declared drift gates. Those are
completed negative observations, not untested suggestions.

The subsequent [synchronized stage profile](../../benchmarks/analysis/results/mlx-profile77-b8.json)
passed the same cohort parity gate. Its diagnostic fractions were MLP `49.74%`
and attention block `40.14%` (the latter includes projections/norm/RoPE/output,
not only SDPA), versus encoding `0.44%` and head `0.12%`. The fenced path took
`3.309s` versus ordinary `2.800s`, an `18.17%` instrumentation increase. These
conditional observations support testing block projections first, but cannot
identify individual kernel time or measured DRAM bandwidth. Removing the whole
MLP diagnostic fraction would cap speedup at `1.990×`; removing head alone at
`1.0012×`. Projection packing affects only part of those blocks.

## Transferable mechanisms and integration boundaries

| Mechanism | Observed upstream behavior | Transfer to Wyat and cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Packed projections | vLLM and SGLang combine Q/K/V in one linear projection; combine gate/up in one MLP projection; apply fused SiLU multiplication. | Small, typed MLX projection adapter using maintained linear kernels is plausible. Concatenate original weights once at load, split outputs in their original order, and release duplicate storage. FLOPs and weight bytes are unchanged; fewer launches/input reads and different GEMM shapes are the hypothesis. |
| Fused elementwise work | vLLM carries residual separately through RMSNorm; MLX-LM already uses fast attention/RoPE/norm and compiled SwiGLU. | Profile residual/add/norm launch fraction before introducing a kernel. Counting an already-used fused primitive as a new improvement would overstate the result. |
| Packed variable-length prefill | vLLM/SGLang model forward paths operate on scheduler token batches and reconstruct per-request boundaries. | Can reduce padding versus a rectangular batch. Requires attention metadata, request ordering and endpoint translation, not just concatenating requests. Medium-to-high integration cost compared with length bucketing inside the current engine. |
| Prefix reuse | Semantic Router's opt-in shared-context path reuses the actual causal prefix before independent question suffixes. | Useful only when the token prefix is truly identical. Menus occur after the query in Kai; repeated menu text is not generally a reusable KV prefix. Token-ID caching remains different from hidden-state/KV caching. |
| Graph replay | Semantic Router captures exact padded shapes on ROCm with bounded retained outputs and explicit fallbacks. | CUDA/HIP graph mechanisms do not transfer directly to Metal. Local MLX whole-function compilation already failed to establish benefit. A graph hypothesis needs measured launch overhead and enough shape reuse to amortize capture. |

The first row follows the pinned [vLLM Qwen3 implementation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387/vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3.py)
and [SGLang MLP implementation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e/python/sglang/srt/models/qwen2.py).
The shared-context and graph rows follow inspected released Semantic Router
source; its MI325X break-even thresholds and gfx942/Transformers guards are
hardware-specific observations, not portable Wyat settings.

vLLM has a pooling runner, including token embeddings. Its stock LAST/ALL/STEP
readouts are not Kai's grouped candidate/query head; STEP selects token IDs,
not arbitrary caller endpoint indices. A future adapter must request raw
hidden states, disable unwanted embedding activation/normalization and apply
the original head before transferring small scores to the host. Sending all
token vectors over HTTP would add avoidable transfer and serialization work.
The official pooling documentation explicitly declines a general performance
guarantee over Transformers. [Pooling models](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/pooling_models/)

SGLang's standard Qwen3 embedding path uses normalized LAST pooling. However,
the pinned [pooler](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e/python/sglang/srt/layers/pooler.py)
also has `token_indices_to_pool`: gather exactly at per-request positions and
optionally return raw pooled hidden states. This is a useful narrow integration
boundary. Its score-head call is flat/per-position; Kai must regroup candidate
rows and each final query row before its shared head. Cache hits/chunked prefill
must not hide requested endpoint states. SGLang's newer
[`/v1/decisions`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e/docs/docs/supported-models/decision_models.mdx)
uses next-token label scoring for chat models; naming alone does not make it a
Kai implementation.

On Mac, the smallest maintained-kernel route remains native MLX. vLLM documents
experimental Apple Silicon **CPU** support requiring a source build, and points
to the community-maintained Metal plugin. The plugin's current experimental
decoder pooling accepts LAST embeddings and a specific Qwen3 reranker; it
explicitly rejects generic heads, decoder ALL/STEP and generic token pooling.
That prevents a drop-in endpoint-aware Kai deployment.
[vLLM CPU installation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation/cpu/),
[Metal pooling contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-metal/blob/2fd759dbd1171a77f7889d04a3b6d75c78fbeea3/docs/text_embedding_pooling.md)

SGLang's inspected CPU recipe targets Intel Xeon AMX. It establishes no Apple
Metal support. Its GPU kernels/scheduler remain relevant to a later supported
GPU comparison, but that comparison has not run here.
[CPU recipe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e/docs/docs/hardware-platforms/cpu_server.mdx)

Batch invariance is a separate contract from equality to a particular reference.
vLLM's beta invariant mode has specific NVIDIA/XPU support and performance
tradeoffs; SGLang's deterministic mode supports FlashInfer/FA3/Triton. Neither
establishes FP32 Metal equality. Packing projections, changing batch shape or
attention kernels can change reductions even when real-number algebra agrees.
Compare raw logits, probabilities, all ranks and tie behavior after each change.
[vLLM invariant mode](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/138810056093301f4881050fcf2b1786939da387/docs/features/batch_invariance.md),
[SGLang deterministic mode](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/b792228b35b21565067520857319dfc05e4d134e/docs/docs/advanced_features/deterministic_inference.mdx)

## Ranked hypotheses and falsifiers

1. **Projection packing:** fewer launches and larger GEMMs improve the measured
   attention/MLP projection fraction. Test QKV and gate/up separately, then
   together, at fixed FP32/weights/tokens/batches. Reject for failed drift gates,
   extra steady memory, or no repeatable full-cohort improvement. Qwen3's query
   width is `16 × 128 = 2048`, while hidden width is 1024 and each K/V width is
   `8 × 128 = 1024`; packing must not assume query width equals hidden width.
   This affects every layer and has a larger possible ceiling than final-layer
   pruning, but no speedup is established by source inspection.
2. **Batch shape efficiency:** distinguish amortized model weight reads from
   padding waste. Sweep six ready-work batch sizes `1,2,4,8,16,32`, retain token
   lengths and complete cohort wall times, then perturb only length grouping.
   Restore caller order and check ranks. Ready-batch throughput is not serving
   latency; a scheduler must also account for admission delay and fairness.
   Reject if gain comes from a changed workload, dropped failures or unmet
   latency constraints.
3. **Selective final-layer readout:** after all earlier layers, compute final
   K/V for all positions; compute queries/output projection/MLP/final norm only
   for candidate/query endpoints. Token-local norms and MLP permit this in real
   arithmetic. Preserve each endpoint's original RoPE position and use explicit
   masks `key_position <= original_query_position`. MLX's causal string uses
   lower-right alignment when query length differs from key length; using it
   for arbitrary selected rows is incorrect. Retain native GQA K/V grouping.
   Explicit masks may change fused dispatch and erase arithmetic savings.
   [MLX SDPA contract](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/python/_autosummary/mlx.core.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention.html)
   RoPE accepts one start offset per batch example, not arbitrary per-token
   positions. Applying full-query RoPE before gathering preserves the maintained
   path but saves less work. Treating each selected query as a length-one batch
   example with its original offset is another testable route, not an established
   performance improvement. [MLX RoPE contract](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/python/_autosummary/mlx.core.fast.rope.html)
   Reject unless endpoint logits pass and measured full-call speed survives.
   Dropping earlier non-endpoint rows is invalid: later layers need their K/V.
4. **Shared actual prefixes:** only after a workload exhibits repeated prefixes
   long enough to dominate prefill. Preserve causal suffix isolation, rotary
   positions and requested cached endpoint states. Freeze a cache key including
   artifact identity and token IDs, bound lifetime/memory, and perturb near ties.
   A margin-triggered fallback is additional policy, not exact equivalence; it
   needs independent validation before becoming a production contract.

## Amdahl, roofline and scaling interpretation

The explanatory tools in `benchmarks/analysis/scaling.py` are candidate models.
For a measured time fraction `f` accelerated by `s`, predicted whole-call
speedup is `1 / (1-f+f/s)`. Even removing the **entire** last block of 28 equally
costly blocks gives only `28/27 ≈ 1.037×`; selective final-layer work saves less.
Use the actual measured fraction, including host work, to replace this rough
assumption. A 20× fixed-workload improvement requires eliminating at least 95%
of baseline time; finite acceleration requires affecting more than 95%.

For Kai's measured shape, one layer's projection parameter count is
`H(Q+2K) + QH + 3HI = 15,728,640`, with `H=1024,Q=2048,K=1024,I=3072`.
Projection FLOPs are `2 × padded_tokens × layers × parameter_count`.
Dense attention FLOPs are `4 × B × layers × query_heads × head_dim × T²`;
ideal triangular causal work is `2 × B × layers × query_heads × head_dim × T(T+1)`.
These exclude norms/RoPE/softmax/head and do not assert a kernel's actual tiling.
Fused projection packing changes neither projection arithmetic nor weight bytes.
Roofline lower bounds need justified device/dtype throughput upper bounds and
actual traffic lower bounds. Summing synchronized microphase timings can
inflate overhead; compare the instrumented whole call with an ordinary control.

Gunther's USL is `C(N)=N/[1+σ(N-1)+κN(N-1)]`, with an interior maximum
`sqrt((1-σ)/κ)` when `κ>0`. Its queue-theoretic interpretation relates
serialization and state-dependent pairwise costs to a synchronous
machine-repairman bound. The paper also discusses paging/thrashing as retrograde
behavior. [Gunther, arXiv:0808.1431v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1431v2)
For this single-GPU batch sweep, `N` is examples per call rather than physical
processors: GEMM shape, padding and memory reuse all change. A fitted positive
`κ` therefore cannot identify cache coherence. This application is descriptive,
an inference limitation rather than a new claim from the paper. Retain residuals,
unconstrained estimates, repeated measurements and ill-conditioning warnings;
negative or weak fits are inconclusive. A predicted optimum outside measured
loads is extrapolation. Follow the user's
[collection guidance](https://teilo.xyz/collections/universal-scaling-law/)
for at least six warmed, steady-state loads, then use traces and one-factor
perturbations to distinguish bandwidth, padding, kernel dispatch, launch overhead
and contention. Do not force coefficients into a preferred causal story.

No vLLM/SGLang integration, GPU execution, new precision policy or 20× inference
claim was validated by this investigation. The supported result is a set of
source-grounded experiments with explicit contracts and rejection conditions.
