# CPU projection packing primitive

The hypothesis is that one maintained FP32 linear operation for K/V or Q/K/V
reduces layer-zero projection cost. This is a primitive test, before a whole-model
candidate. Numerical and full-ranking model parity remain hard constraints.

The existing captured gate inputs are post-attention MLP activations and are not
QKV inputs. Instead, read the exact released checkpoint through Safetensors mmap:
only the required embedding rows, layer-zero input RMSNorm and Q/K/V weights.
Apply maintained Qwen3RMSNorm with epsilon `1e-6` to the authoritative full token
vectors, then take suffix rows after the exact 25-token prefix. This norm is
per-token; preceding attention is absent in layer zero. No backbone is created or
executed. Pinned tokenizer metadata resolves padding to token `151643`.

The four fixed operands are canonical offsets 7/18/75 (full lengths 192/197/214,
suffix lengths 167/172/189) and the canonical first eight requests, padded to 192
before normalization and prefix removal (B8 suffix length 167). Preserve token
IDs, case IDs, ordering, padding, activation bytes, shapes and strides. All 77
reference vectors and canonical inputs are admitted before checkpoint tensors.
These are BANKING77 training-source development cases; checkpoint exposure is
unknown.

Q/K/V have output widths 2048/1024/1024 and input width 1024. One FP32 packed
allocation is 16 MiB. Separate Q/K/V use contiguous views; packed KV uses its
contiguous tail; packed QKV uses the complete allocation. Original source tensors
are released after exact-bit checks. The temporary source-plus-packed projection
pool is 32 MiB during setup, excluding normalization, activations, output archives
and allocator storage. This is logical capacity, not RSS. Hypothetical 28-layer
QKV and KV copies would be 448/224 MiB if originals were also retained; this
primitive does not create those copies.

Every arm executes one cold call, one warm call and six measured calls, following
all six permutations of `separate`, `kv`, `qkv`: 96 total calls across four
operands. The clock contains one `project()` call, including admission, maintained
`F.linear` and output splitting. Setup, hashing, snapshots, quality comparisons
and persistence occur outside that clock. Each call's output shapes, strides,
bytes hash and raw timing are retained before its gate can reject it. Save each
distinct output and input in an excluded local Safetensors artifact. Changed
strides may affect later Q/K normalization or RoPE; neither is timed here.

Projection parity uses the original symmetric max allowance:
`abs(a-b) <= max(1e-3, 1e-3 * max(abs(a), abs(b)))`, with finite FP32 outputs.
There is no probability or full-ranking claim at this boundary. The unchanged
whole-model gates remain mandatory for any later candidate.

A candidate is eligible for a later full-model screen only if all four operands
have six-order median baseline/candidate ratio at least **1.12** and interpolated
sample p05 strictly above **1.0**. This prospective filter is not promotion. A
historical profiled projection fraction of 0.1938 motivates conservative triage
under an unchanged-cost assumption; it is not an observed ordinary fraction or
speed bound. Every ratio remains visible, including regressions. Source/assets,
process policy and thread restoration must pass before a positive completion
receipt. No new precision policy, JIT, GPU work or production changes occur.

The command below records the historical launch. Existing receipts must remain
intact; any separately authorized repeat requires a fresh output stem. No repeat
is needed or authorized by these results.

```sh
python -m benchmarks.analysis.torch.projection.run .models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B \
  --output benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive.json
```

The standard-library parent owns one 120-second child process group. Timeout,
failed output, missing call or incomplete receipt is unknown/rejected; do not
rerun or relax gates to hide it. Local primitive timings cannot establish a model,
server or general CPU speed gain. No production promotion is performed.

## Observed result

The repaired bounded worker completed **96 calls** across all four authentic
operands. The independent standard-library audit bound every saved output to its
actual FP32 array and recomputed the unchanged symmetric numerical gate. All
three arms have identical output hashes at every shape, with maximum absolute
and relative differences **zero**. Exact packed projection values match the
released layer-zero Q/K/V tensors after their BF16-to-FP32 expansion.

| Authentic operand | KV median | KV sample p05 | QKV median | QKV sample p05 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scalar, full length 192 | 1.01678x | 0.93591x | 1.07154x | 1.01623x |
| Scalar, full length 197 | 1.02530x | 1.01108x | 1.05531x | 1.04202x |
| Scalar, full length 214 | 1.02920x | 1.00146x | 1.05988x | 1.03029x |
| First eight, padded full length 192 | 1.04164x | 1.00155x | 1.03274x | 0.96456x |

Both variants miss the prospective **1.12x median at every operand** condition.
KV also regresses in the scalar-192 tail, and QKV regresses in the batch-eight
tail. All six ratios per operand and arm remain in the
[raw report](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final.json)
and [independent audit](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final-review.json).
Both `primitive_eligible` values are false; `accepted` remains false. Do not
construct or promote a full-model candidate from this screen. This rejects the
measured packing candidate under this declared filter, without ruling out
another implementation or context. The sample p05 is not a confidence bound.

The inference child exited zero and was reaped after **4.122 s** within its
120-second cap. Source/asset verification and original thread restoration pass.
The independent audit exited zero and was reaped after **3.061 s** within its
separate 60-second cap; its
[execution receipt](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final-review-final.execution.json)
preserves exact producer text, argv, output and ownership. The audit validates
16 executed source texts, the six reviewed experiment files, unchanged
production22 and the pinned input/model assets. The raw report SHA is
`fe4d68337e4b695bdafc26c18ed261bd776175e36e6970ed03694965840afe17`;
the executed source archive SHA is
`eff85f9cc7c03a0d045499df4c984d9747e6c7c23d60efad53c841caf2b97fb6`.
The prospective protocol above remains in that immutable archive; this result
was appended afterward.

Normalized operands are authenticated by source/model/token provenance and
retained byte identities. The auditor does not independently replay Torch's
RMSNorm reduction or recompute every matrix product: separate-projection outputs
are its numerical parity oracle. Input outer strides retain the full-token
width for singleton batches, where that stride is inactive, and use the compact
suffix width for batch eight. Output split strides differ between arms and are
retained explicitly. Q/K normalization, RoPE, attention, cache updates, decision
heads, ranks and probabilities are outside this primitive. Logical allocation
counters do not establish RSS, peak memory, device aliases or whole-model speed.

## Preserved failure history

The initial real worker rejected its own supervisor-created `.wall.json` and
`.log` sidecars before input admission or checkpoint operands. It exited one
without a timeout after **1.799 s**; no main receipt or primitive sample exists.
That attempt is an execution-harness failure with unknown quality and speed.
Its [wall](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive.wall.json) and
[log](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive.log) remain intact.
A narrowly reviewed sidecar allowance plus collision tests preceded the fresh
final run; the repaired focused suite passed **18 tests**.

The first independent raw-audit attempt assumed compact outer input strides even
for singleton batches and stopped before output parity scans. Its
[failed execution receipt](../../../benchmarks/analysis/results/torch-qkv-primitive-final-review.execution.json)
and exact producer remain preserved. The auditor then corrected only that
layout expectation and inspected the same immutable raw arrays successfully;
no model inference was repeated for this auditor correction.

"""Native MLX choice scoring using MLX-LM's maintained Qwen3 backbone.

The checkpoint, segmented tokenizer recipe and FP32 head are shared with the
Torch backend. No language-model vocabulary projection or decoding is executed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

import mlx.core as mx
from mlx.nn.layers.activations import gelu
from mlx.nn.layers.base import Module
from mlx.nn.layers.linear import Linear
from mlx.nn.layers.normalization import LayerNorm
from mlx_lm.models.qwen3 import ModelArgs, Qwen3Model

from wyat.core import Request
from wyat.wire import JsonObject

from .artifact import load_artifact
from .encoding import EncodedRequest, KaiEncoder

Forward = Callable[[mx.array, mx.array, mx.array], mx.array]


class MLXCandidateHead(Module):
    """Released exact-GELU bilinear + MLP readout, entirely in FP32."""

    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, head_dim: int) -> None:
        super().__init__()  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]  # Upstream MLX boundary.
        self.head_dim = head_dim
        self.candidate_norm = LayerNorm(hidden_size, eps=1e-5)
        self.query_norm = LayerNorm(hidden_size, eps=1e-5)
        self.key = Linear(hidden_size, head_dim, bias=False)
        self.query = Linear(hidden_size, head_dim, bias=False)
        self.candidate_mlp = Linear(hidden_size, head_dim)
        self.query_mlp = Linear(hidden_size, head_dim, bias=False)
        self.scalar = Linear(head_dim, 1, bias=False)

    def __call__(self, candidates: mx.array, query: mx.array) -> mx.array:
        candidate = cast(mx.array, self.candidate_norm(candidates.astype(mx.float32)))
        global_query = cast(mx.array, self.query_norm(query.astype(mx.float32)))
        bilinear = mx.sum(
            self.key(candidate) * self.query(global_query)[:, None, :], axis=-1
        ) / math.sqrt(self.head_dim)
        nonlinear = self.scalar(
            gelu(
                self.candidate_mlp(candidate) + self.query_mlp(global_query)[:, None, :]
            )
        ).squeeze(-1)
        return bilinear + nonlinear


def _weights(path: Path, *, head: bool) -> dict[str, mx.array]:
    loaded: object = mx.load(str(path))
    if not isinstance(loaded, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected named checkpoint tensors: {path.name}")
    weights = cast(dict[str, mx.array], loaded)
    for name, value in weights.items():
        allowed = {mx.float32} if head else {mx.float32, mx.bfloat16}
        if value.dtype not in allowed:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported {'head' if head else 'backbone'} dtype: {name}"
            )
        # Keep validation temporary arrays bounded for large embedding tables.
        flat = value.reshape(-1)
        for start in range(0, flat.size, 1 << 20):
            if not bool(mx.all(mx.isfinite(flat[start : start + (1 << 20)])).item()):
                raise ValueError(f"Nonfinite checkpoint tensor: {name}")
        weights[name] = value.astype(mx.float32)
    return weights


class MLXKaiScorer:
    """Immutable local weights; causal batched prefill and endpoint readout."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        backbone: Qwen3Model,
        head: MLXCandidateHead,
        encoder: KaiEncoder,
        *,
        model_id: str,
        device: mx.Device,
        compile: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        if type(compile) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("compile must be a boolean")
        self.backbone = backbone
        self.head = head
        self.encoder = encoder
        self.model_id = model_id
        self.device = device
        self._compiled = compile
        self._forward: Forward = (
            cast(Forward, mx.compile(self._logits)) if self._compiled else self._logits
        )

    @property
    def compiled(self) -> bool:
        return self._compiled

    @classmethod
    def from_directory(
        cls,
        path: str | Path,
        *,
        max_length: int = 2048,
        token_cache_size: int = 0,
        device: str = "gpu",
        compile: bool = False,
    ) -> MLXKaiScorer:
        if device not in {"cpu", "gpu"}:
            raise ValueError("MLX device must be cpu or gpu")
        if device == "gpu" and not mx.metal.is_available():
            raise ValueError("MLX GPU inference requires available Apple Metal")
        if type(compile) is not bool:
            raise ValueError("compile must be a boolean")
        artifact = load_artifact(path, max_length=max_length)
        encoder = KaiEncoder.from_artifact(
            artifact,
            max_length=max_length,
            token_cache_size=token_cache_size,
        )
        target = mx.Device(mx.gpu if device == "gpu" else mx.cpu)
        with mx.stream(target):
            arguments = cast(Callable[[JsonObject], ModelArgs], ModelArgs.from_dict)
            args = arguments(artifact.config)
            backbone = Qwen3Model(args)
            head = MLXCandidateHead(args.hidden_size, artifact.head_dim)
            backbone_weights = _weights(
                artifact.root / "backbone/model.safetensors", head=False
            )
            head_weights = _weights(
                artifact.root / "decision_head.safetensors", head=True
            )
            backbone.load_weights(list(backbone_weights.items()), strict=True)
            head.load_weights(list(head_weights.items()), strict=True)
            backbone.eval()
            head.eval()
            mx.eval(backbone_weights, head_weights)
        return cls(
            backbone,
            head,
            encoder,
            model_id=artifact.model_id,
            device=target,
            compile=compile,
        )

    def encode_request(self, request: Request) -> EncodedRequest:
        return self.encoder.encode_request(request)

    def _logits(
        self, ids: mx.array, endpoints: mx.array, query_positions: mx.array
    ) -> mx.array:
        # Right padding cannot influence an earlier endpoint in a causal model.
        hidden = cast(mx.array, self.backbone(ids))
        rows = mx.arange(ids.shape[0])
        return self.head(
            hidden[rows[:, None], endpoints], hidden[rows, query_positions]
        )

    def score_many(self, requests: Sequence[Request]) -> list[list[float]]:
        if not requests:
            return []
        encoded = [self.encode_request(request) for request in requests]
        with mx.stream(self.device):
            ids, endpoints, positions = _pack(encoded, self.encoder.pad_id)
            logits = self._forward(ids, endpoints, positions)
            mx.eval(logits)
            values = cast(list[list[float]], logits.tolist())
        return [
            row[: len(item.candidate_positions)]
            for row, item in zip(values, encoded, strict=True)
        ]


def _pack(
    encoded: Sequence[EncodedRequest], pad_id: int, *, prefix_length: int = 0
) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array, mx.array]:
    """One native packing owner; retain full padded width when removing prefix."""
    length = -(-max(len(row.ids) for row in encoded) // 8) * 8
    width = max(len(row.candidate_positions) for row in encoded)
    ids = mx.array(
        [
            list(row.ids[prefix_length:]) + [pad_id] * (length - len(row.ids))
            for row in encoded
        ],
        dtype=mx.int32,
    )
    endpoints = mx.array(
        [
            [position - prefix_length for position in row.candidate_positions]
            + [0] * (width - len(row.candidate_positions))
            for row in encoded
        ],
        dtype=mx.int32,
    )
    positions = mx.array(
        [row.query_position - prefix_length for row in encoded], dtype=mx.int32
    )
    return ids, endpoints, positions

"""Selected final Qwen3 readouts with original causal and rotary positions."""

# Portions adapted from MLX-LM Qwen3, Copyright © 2023–2024 Apple Inc.
# MIT License; the complete permission notice is included in repository NOTICE.

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
from typing import Protocol, cast

import mlx.core as mx
from mlx.nn.layers.linear import Linear
from mlx_lm.models.base import create_attention_mask
from mlx_lm.models.qwen3 import Qwen3Model, TransformerBlock

type ArrayMap = Callable[[mx.array], mx.array]


class RotaryMap(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, x: mx.array, offset: int | mx.array = 0) -> mx.array: ...


class AttentionWeights(Protocol):
    n_heads: int
    n_kv_heads: int
    scale: float
    q_proj: Linear
    k_proj: Linear
    v_proj: Linear
    o_proj: Linear
    q_norm: ArrayMap
    k_norm: ArrayMap
    rope: RotaryMap


class EndpointCache(Protocol):
    offset: int

    def update_and_fetch(
        self, keys: mx.array, values: mx.array
    ) -> tuple[mx.array, mx.array]: ...


def endpoint_last_block(
    block: TransformerBlock,
    hidden: mx.array,
    positions: mx.array,
    cache: EndpointCache | None = None,
) -> mx.array:
    """Select suffix rows, retaining cached K/V and absolute causal positions."""
    batch, length, _ = hidden.shape
    offset = 0 if cache is None else cache.offset
    absolute_positions = positions + offset
    rows = mx.arange(batch)[:, None]
    residual = hidden[rows, positions]
    normalize = cast(ArrayMap, block.input_layernorm)
    normalized = normalize(hidden)
    selected = normalized[rows, positions]
    attention = cast(AttentionWeights, block.self_attn)
    count = positions.shape[1]
    queries = attention.q_norm(
        attention.q_proj(selected).reshape(batch, count, attention.n_heads, -1)
    )
    dimension = queries.shape[-1]
    # Treat each original endpoint as a separate one-token sequence. Native
    # RoPE accepts one offset per batch row, preserving nonconsecutive positions.
    queries = (
        attention.rope(
            queries.reshape(batch * count, attention.n_heads, 1, dimension),
            offset=absolute_positions.reshape(-1),
        )
        .reshape(batch, count, attention.n_heads, dimension)
        .transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
    )
    keys = attention.k_norm(
        attention.k_proj(normalized).reshape(batch, length, attention.n_kv_heads, -1)
    ).transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
    keys = attention.rope(keys, offset=offset)
    values = (
        attention.v_proj(normalized)
        .reshape(batch, length, attention.n_kv_heads, dimension)
        .transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
    )
    if cache is not None:
        keys, values = cache.update_and_fetch(keys, values)
    mask = (
        mx.arange(keys.shape[2])[None, None, None, :]
        <= absolute_positions[:, None, :, None]
    )
    attended = (
        mx.fast.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            queries, keys, values, scale=attention.scale, mask=mask
        )
        .transpose(0, 2, 1, 3)
        .reshape(batch, count, -1)
    )
    residual = residual + attention.o_proj(attended)
    post_normalize = cast(ArrayMap, block.post_attention_layernorm)
    mlp = cast(ArrayMap, block.mlp)
    return residual + mlp(post_normalize(residual))


class CachedBlock(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self, hidden: mx.array, mask: str | mx.array | None, cache: EndpointCache
    ) -> mx.array: ...


attention_mask = cast(
    Callable[[mx.array, EndpointCache], str | mx.array | None], create_attention_mask
)


def cached_endpoint_hidden(
    backbone: Qwen3Model,
    ids: mx.array,
    positions: mx.array,
    caches: Sequence[EndpointCache],
) -> mx.array:
    """Use upstream cached early blocks, then selected final suffix readouts."""
    if backbone.args.rope_scaling is not None:
        raise ValueError("Endpoint readout requires unscaled native RoPE")
    if len(caches) != len(backbone.layers) or not caches:
        raise ValueError("One fresh prefix cache is required per maintained layer")
    if any(cache.offset != caches[0].offset for cache in caches):
        raise ValueError("All caches must start at the same original prefix offset")
    hidden = backbone.embed_tokens(ids)
    mask = attention_mask(hidden, caches[0])
    blocks = cast(Sequence[CachedBlock], backbone.layers[:-1])
    for block, cache in zip(blocks, caches[:-1], strict=True):
        hidden = block(hidden, mask, cache)
    hidden = endpoint_last_block(backbone.layers[-1], hidden, positions, caches[-1])
    normalize = cast(ArrayMap, backbone.norm)
    return normalize(hidden)

"""PyTorch CPU/CUDA inference for the released candidate-aware Kai contract.

Adapted from Decision 2.0 at cd49ea3813fd8ba0928a9a23ef6c9a0f2f0cd764.
Artifact validation and segmented input belong to artifact and encoding. This
module owns tensor loading, the FP32 candidate head, and causal execution.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from collections.abc import Sequence
from contextlib import nullcontext
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

import torch
from safetensors import SafetensorError
from safetensors.torch import load_file
from torch import nn
from torch.nn import functional as F
from transformers import Qwen3Config, Qwen3Model
from transformers.cache_utils import DynamicCache
from transformers.modeling_outputs import BaseModelOutputWithPast

from wyat.core import Request
from wyat.wire import JsonObject

from .artifact import ARCHITECTURE as ARCHITECTURE
from .artifact import PROMPT_VERSION as PROMPT_VERSION
from .artifact import load_artifact, normalize_config, positive_integer
from .encoding import EncodedRequest as EncodedRequest
from .encoding import KaiEncoder, TokenizerProtocol, load_tokenizer


def _config(raw: JsonObject) -> Qwen3Config:
    return Qwen3Config.from_dict(normalize_config(raw))


class CandidateHead(nn.Module):
    """The released FP32 bilinear plus nonlinear per-candidate readout."""

    def __init__(self, hidden_size: int, head_dim: int = 256) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.head_dim = head_dim
        self.candidate_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
        self.query_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_size)
        self.key = nn.Linear(hidden_size, head_dim, bias=False)
        self.query = nn.Linear(hidden_size, head_dim, bias=False)
        self.candidate_mlp = nn.Linear(hidden_size, head_dim)
        self.query_mlp = nn.Linear(hidden_size, head_dim, bias=False)
        self.scalar = nn.Linear(head_dim, 1, bias=False)

    def forward(self, candidates: torch.Tensor, query: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        with torch.autocast(device_type=candidates.device.type, enabled=False):
            candidate = self.candidate_norm(candidates.float())
            global_query = self.query_norm(query.float())
            bilinear = (self.key(candidate) * self.query(global_query)[:, None, :]).sum(
                -1
            ) / math.sqrt(self.head_dim)
            nonlinear = self.scalar(
                F.gelu(
                    self.candidate_mlp(candidate)
                    + self.query_mlp(global_query)[:, None, :]
                )
            ).squeeze(-1)
            return cast(torch.Tensor, bilinear + nonlinear)


def _finite_tensor(value: torch.Tensor, name: str) -> None:
    # Keep the temporary boolean allocation below 1 MiB, including embeddings.
    flattened = value.detach().reshape(-1)
    for start in range(0, flattened.numel(), 1 << 20):
        chunk = flattened[start : start + (1 << 20)]
        if not torch.isfinite(chunk).all().item():
            raise ValueError(f"Nonfinite checkpoint tensor: {name}")


class KaiScorer(KaiEncoder):
    """Immutable CPU/CUDA weights with the shared entry-bounded input encoder."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        backbone: Qwen3Model,
        head: CandidateHead,
        tokenizer: TokenizerProtocol,
        *,
        device: torch.device,
        max_length: int,
        max_options: int,
        token_cache_size: int,
        model_id: str,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            tokenizer,
            max_length=max_length,
            max_options=max_options,
            token_cache_size=token_cache_size,
        )
        self.backbone = backbone
        self.head = head
        self.device = device
        self.model_id = model_id

    @classmethod
    def from_directory(
        cls,
        path: str | Path,
        *,
        device: str = "cpu",
        max_length: int = 2048,
        token_cache_size: int = 0,
        attention: str = "sdpa",
    ) -> KaiScorer:
        if attention not in {"sdpa", "eager"}:
            raise ValueError("attention must be sdpa or eager")
        target = torch.device(device)
        if target.type not in {"cpu", "cuda"}:
            raise ValueError("Kai currently supports cpu and cuda devices")
        if target.type == "cuda" and (
            not torch.cuda.is_available() or not torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported()
        ):
            raise ValueError("CUDA/ROCm inference requires a BF16-capable GPU")
        artifact = load_artifact(path, max_length)
        tokenizer = load_tokenizer(artifact.root)
        config = _config(artifact.config)
        try:
            backbone, loading = cast(
                tuple[Qwen3Model, dict[str, object]],
                Qwen3Model.from_pretrained(
                    artifact.root / "backbone",
                    config=config,
                    dtype=torch.float32,
                    local_files_only=True,
                    trust_remote_code=False,
                    use_safetensors=True,
                    attn_implementation=attention,
                    output_loading_info=True,
                ),
            )
        except SafetensorError as error:
            raise ValueError("Malformed Kai backbone Safetensors weights") from error
        if any(
            loading.get(key)
            for key in (
                "missing_keys",
                "unexpected_keys",
                "mismatched_keys",
                "error_msgs",
            )
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Backbone weights do not match their configuration: {loading}"
            )
        for name, parameter in backbone.named_parameters():
            _finite_tensor(parameter, name)
        for name, buffer in backbone.named_buffers():
            _finite_tensor(buffer, name)
        head = CandidateHead(
            positive_integer(artifact.config.get("hidden_size"), "hidden_size"),
            artifact.head_dim,
        )
        try:
            head_state = load_file(artifact.root / "decision_head.safetensors")
        except SafetensorError as error:
            raise ValueError("Malformed Kai head Safetensors weights") from error
        for name, tensor in head_state.items():
            _finite_tensor(tensor, name)
        head.load_state_dict(head_state, strict=True)
        # Restore only losslessly representable Linear weights to the released
        # BF16 storage recipe; embeddings, norms, residuals and head stay FP32.
        if target.type == "cuda":
            for layer in backbone.modules():
                if isinstance(layer, nn.Linear):
                    for linear_parameter in (layer.weight, layer.bias):
                        if linear_parameter is not None:
                            rounded = linear_parameter.detach().to(torch.bfloat16)
                            if torch.equal(rounded.float(), linear_parameter.detach()):
                                linear_parameter.data = rounded
        backbone.config.use_cache = False
        cast(nn.Module, backbone).to(target)
        cast(nn.Module, backbone).eval()
        return cls(
            backbone,
            head.to(target).eval(),
            tokenizer,
            device=target,
            max_length=max_length,
            max_options=artifact.max_options,
            token_cache_size=token_cache_size,
            model_id=artifact.model_id,
        )

    def score_many(self, requests: Sequence[Request]) -> list[list[float]]:
        if not requests:
            return []
        encoded = [self.encode_request(request) for request in requests]
        return self._score_encoded(encoded)

    def _score_encoded(
        self,
        encoded: Sequence[EncodedRequest],
        *,
        prefix_length: int = 0,
        cache: DynamicCache | None = None,
    ) -> list[list[float]]:
        """One tensor/readout owner for fully admitted original request rows."""
        if not encoded:
            return []
        if cache is None:
            if prefix_length != 0:
                raise ValueError("Removing prefix tokens requires a seeded cache")
        elif (
            self.device.type != "cpu"
            or type(cache) is not DynamicCache
            or type(prefix_length) is not int
            or prefix_length <= 0
            or cache.get_seq_length() != prefix_length
        ):
            raise ValueError("Cached scoring requires a seeded CPU DynamicCache")
        length = max(len(row.ids) for row in encoded) - prefix_length
        width = max(len(row.candidate_positions) for row in encoded)
        batch_size = len(encoded)
        ids = torch.full((batch_size, length), self.pad_id, dtype=torch.long)
        endpoints = torch.zeros((batch_size, width), dtype=torch.long)
        for index, row in enumerate(encoded):
            suffix = row.ids[prefix_length:]
            ids[index, : len(suffix)] = torch.tensor(suffix, dtype=torch.long)
            endpoints[index, : len(row.candidate_positions)] = torch.tensor(
                [position - prefix_length for position in row.candidate_positions]
            )
        ids, endpoints = (value.to(self.device) for value in (ids, endpoints))
        rows = torch.arange(batch_size, device=self.device)
        query_positions = torch.tensor(
            [row.query_position - prefix_length for row in encoded], device=self.device
        )
        autocast = (
            torch.autocast(device_type="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
            if self.device.type == "cuda"
            else nullcontext()
        )
        with torch.inference_mode(), autocast:
            # Every readout precedes right padding. Causality excludes those
            # future pads, so a separate padding mask cannot affect the readout.
            if cache is None:
                output = cast(
                    BaseModelOutputWithPast,
                    self.backbone(input_ids=ids, use_cache=False),
                )
            else:
                # HF owns the absolute RoPE positions and rectangular offset
                # mask. An unmasked rectangular is_causal call is not equivalent.
                output = cast(
                    BaseModelOutputWithPast,
                    self.backbone(input_ids=ids, past_key_values=cache, use_cache=True),
                )
            hidden = output.last_hidden_state
            if hidden is None:
                raise ValueError("Kai backbone did not return hidden states")
            logits = cast(
                torch.Tensor,
                self.head(
                    hidden[rows[:, None], endpoints], hidden[rows, query_positions]
                ),
            )
        values = cast(list[list[float]], logits.float().cpu().tolist())
        return [
            row[: len(item.candidate_positions)]
            for row, item in zip(values, encoded, strict=True)
        ]

"""Paired, synchronized engine measurements with failure-inclusive quality gates."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import platform
import resource
import sys
import time
from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version

from .core import Model
from .evaluation import EvaluationCase, EvaluationRow, _input_digest, percentile


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class QualityGate:
    """Declare tolerances before measuring; default acceptance preserves every rank."""

    logit_atol: float = 1e-3
    logit_rtol: float = 1e-3
    probability_atol: float = 1e-4

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if any(
            isinstance(value, bool) or not math.isfinite(value) or value < 0
            for value in (self.logit_atol, self.logit_rtol, self.probability_atol)
        ):
            raise ValueError("quality tolerances must be finite and nonnegative")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BenchmarkProtocol:
    repeats: int = 5
    warmup: int = 1
    quality_gate: QualityGate = field(default_factory=QualityGate)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if type(self.repeats) is not int or self.repeats < 3:
            raise ValueError("benchmark requires at least three repetitions")
        if type(self.warmup) is not int or self.warmup < 1:
            raise ValueError("benchmark requires at least one warmup cycle")


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BenchmarkEngine:
    name: str
    model: Model
    batch_size: int = 1
    conditions: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    synchronize: Callable[[], None] | None = None

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.name.strip():
            raise ValueError("engine name must be nonempty")
        if type(self.batch_size) is not int or self.batch_size < 1:
            raise ValueError("engine batch_size must be a positive integer")


def process_peak_rss_bytes() -> int:
    """OS process high-water RSS, cumulative across both loaded engines and arms."""
    peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
    return int(peak if sys.platform == "darwin" else peak * 1024)


def _versions() -> dict[str, str]:
    installed: dict[str, str] = {}
    for package in (
        "wyat",
        "torch",
        "transformers",
        "tokenizers",
        "safetensors",
        "mlx",
        "mlx-lm",
    ):
        try:
            installed[package] = version(package)
        except PackageNotFoundError:
            continue
    return installed


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BenchmarkCycle:
    latency_ms: float
    rows: tuple[EvaluationRow, ...]
    peak_rss_before_bytes: int
    peak_rss_after_bytes: int

    @property
    def correct(self) -> int:
        return sum(row.correct for row in self.rows)

    @property
    def failed(self) -> int:
        return sum(row.status != "ok" for row in self.rows)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "latency_ms": self.latency_ms,
            "peak_rss_before_bytes": self.peak_rss_before_bytes,
            "peak_rss_after_bytes": self.peak_rss_after_bytes,
            "correct": self.correct,
            "failed": self.failed,
            "rows": [row.to_dict() for row in self.rows],
        }


def _run(engine: BenchmarkEngine, cases: tuple[EvaluationCase, ...]) -> BenchmarkCycle:
    # Native Wyat scorers return host floats. Other scorers can provide a barrier.
    if engine.synchronize is not None:
        engine.synchronize()
    peak_before = process_peak_rss_bytes()
    start = time.perf_counter_ns()
    rows: list[EvaluationRow] = []
    for offset in range(0, len(cases), engine.batch_size):
        batch = cases[offset : offset + engine.batch_size]
        batch_start = time.perf_counter_ns()
        try:
            predictions = engine.model.decide_many(
                tuple(case.request for case in batch)
            )
            if engine.synchronize is not None:
                engine.synchronize()
        except Exception as error:
            latency = (time.perf_counter_ns() - batch_start) / 1_000_000
            rows.extend(
                EvaluationRow(
                    case.id,
                    case.expected,
                    "error",
                    None,
                    False,
                    latency,
                    f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
                )
                for case in batch
            )
        else:
            latency = (time.perf_counter_ns() - batch_start) / 1_000_000
            rows.extend(
                EvaluationRow(
                    case.id,
                    case.expected,
                    "ok",
                    prediction,
                    prediction.selected in case.expected,
                    latency,
                    None,
                )
                for case, prediction in zip(batch, predictions, strict=True)
            )
    elapsed = (time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1_000_000
    return BenchmarkCycle(elapsed, tuple(rows), peak_before, process_peak_rss_bytes())


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DriftReport:
    total: int
    comparable: int
    selected_equal: int
    ranking_equal: int
    baseline_correct: int
    candidate_correct: int
    max_abs_logit_difference: float | None
    max_abs_probability_difference: float | None
    logits_within_tolerance: bool
    probabilities_within_tolerance: bool
    passed: bool


def compare_cycles(
    baseline: Sequence[BenchmarkCycle],
    candidate: Sequence[BenchmarkCycle],
    gate: QualityGate,
) -> DriftReport:
    """Compare aligned repetitions; every missing or failed result fails the gate."""
    if not baseline or len(baseline) != len(candidate):
        raise ValueError("paired nonempty cycles with identical counts required")
    total = comparable = selected = ranked = base_correct = cand_correct = 0
    logit_differences: list[float] = []
    probability_differences: list[float] = []
    logits_close = probabilities_close = True
    for left_cycle, right_cycle in zip(baseline, candidate, strict=True):
        if not left_cycle.rows or len(left_cycle.rows) != len(right_cycle.rows):
            raise ValueError("paired cycles require identical nonempty case counts")
        for left, right in zip(left_cycle.rows, right_cycle.rows, strict=True):
            if left.id != right.id or left.expected != right.expected:
                raise ValueError("paired cycle IDs and labels must match")
            total += 1
            base_correct += left.correct
            cand_correct += right.correct
            if left.prediction is None or right.prediction is None:
                continue
            a, b = left.prediction, right.prediction
            if len(a.scores) != len(b.scores):
                raise ValueError("paired candidate counts must match")
            comparable += 1
            selected += a.selected == b.selected
            ranked += a.ranking == b.ranking
            for x, y in zip(a.scores, b.scores, strict=True):
                logit_differences.append(abs(x - y))
                logits_close &= math.isclose(
                    x, y, abs_tol=gate.logit_atol, rel_tol=gate.logit_rtol
                )
            for x, y in zip(a.probabilities, b.probabilities, strict=True):
                difference = abs(x - y)
                probability_differences.append(difference)
                probabilities_close &= difference <= gate.probability_atol
    complete = comparable == total
    return DriftReport(
        total,
        comparable,
        selected,
        ranked,
        base_correct,
        cand_correct,
        max(logit_differences, default=None),
        max(probability_differences, default=None),
        complete and logits_close,
        complete and probabilities_close,
        complete
        and selected == total
        and ranked == total
        and logits_close
        and probabilities_close
        and cand_correct >= base_correct,
    )


def _arm_report(
    engine: BenchmarkEngine, cycles: tuple[BenchmarkCycle, ...]
) -> dict[str, object]:
    timings = [cycle.latency_ms for cycle in cycles]
    attempted = sum(len(cycle.rows) for cycle in cycles)
    failed = sum(cycle.failed for cycle in cycles)
    correct = sum(cycle.correct for cycle in cycles)
    batch_latencies = [row.latency_ms for cycle in cycles for row in cycle.rows]
    elapsed_seconds = math.fsum(timings) / 1000
    return {
        "name": engine.name,
        "model_id": engine.model.model_id,
        "conditions": dict(engine.conditions),
        "batch_size": engine.batch_size,
        "attempted": attempted,
        "failed": failed,
        "correct": correct,
        "accuracy": correct / attempted,
        "coverage": (attempted - failed) / attempted,
        "cycle_p50_ms": percentile(timings, 0.50),
        "cycle_p95_ms": percentile(timings, 0.95),
        "batch_residence_p50_ms": percentile(batch_latencies, 0.50),
        "batch_residence_p95_ms": percentile(batch_latencies, 0.95),
        "attempted_requests_per_second": attempted / elapsed_seconds,
        "successful_requests_per_second": (attempted - failed) / elapsed_seconds,
        "cycles": [cycle.to_dict() for cycle in cycles],
    }


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class BenchmarkReport:
    input_sha256: str
    cases: tuple[EvaluationCase, ...]
    protocol: BenchmarkProtocol
    baseline: BenchmarkEngine
    candidate: BenchmarkEngine
    baseline_cycles: tuple[BenchmarkCycle, ...]
    candidate_cycles: tuple[BenchmarkCycle, ...]
    drift: DriftReport
    baseline_warmup_cycles: tuple[BenchmarkCycle, ...]
    candidate_warmup_cycles: tuple[BenchmarkCycle, ...]

    @property
    def warmup_failed(self) -> int:
        return sum(
            cycle.failed
            for cycle in self.baseline_warmup_cycles + self.candidate_warmup_cycles
        )

    @property
    def passed(self) -> bool:
        return self.drift.passed and self.warmup_failed == 0

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        baseline_times = [cycle.latency_ms for cycle in self.baseline_cycles]
        candidate_times = [cycle.latency_ms for cycle in self.candidate_cycles]
        speedups = [
            left / right
            for left, right in zip(baseline_times, candidate_times, strict=True)
        ]
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "input_sha256": self.input_sha256,
            "case_ids": [case.id for case in self.cases],
            "case_count": len(self.cases),
            "environment": {
                "python": platform.python_version(),
                "platform": platform.platform(),
                "machine": platform.machine(),
                "versions": _versions(),
            },
            "protocol": {
                **asdict(self.protocol),
                "paired_order": "alternating baseline/candidate, candidate/baseline",
                "timing": "complete cohort cycles, including tokenization, batching, "
                "model, host results, decision interpretation and row bookkeeping",
                "batch_residence": "full synchronous batch call latency assigned to "
                "each member; excludes admission queue and transport",
                "memory": "OS cumulative process high-water RSS at cycle boundaries; "
                "shared loaded engines, cannot attribute per-arm resident memory",
                "excludes": ["loading", "warmup", "HTTP", "JSON serialization"],
                "native_synchronization": "native scorers materialize host floats; "
                "custom engines may supply an explicit barrier",
            },
            "baseline": _arm_report(self.baseline, self.baseline_cycles),
            "candidate": _arm_report(self.candidate, self.candidate_cycles),
            "quality": asdict(self.drift),
            "warmup": {
                "failed": self.warmup_failed,
                "baseline_cycles": [
                    cycle.to_dict() for cycle in self.baseline_warmup_cycles
                ],
                "candidate_cycles": [
                    cycle.to_dict() for cycle in self.candidate_warmup_cycles
                ],
            },
            "passed": self.passed,
            "speed": {
                "paired_cycle_speedups": speedups,
                "paired_speedup_p50": percentile(speedups, 0.50),
                "paired_speedup_p05": percentile(speedups, 0.05),
                "paired_speedup_p95": percentile(speedups, 0.95),
                "median_speedup_positive": percentile(speedups, 0.50) > 1,
            },
        }


def benchmark_pair(
    baseline: BenchmarkEngine,
    candidate: BenchmarkEngine,
    cases: Sequence[EvaluationCase],
    *,
    protocol: BenchmarkProtocol | None = None,
) -> BenchmarkReport:
    """Freeze inputs and gates, warm both engines, alternate paired measurements."""
    plan = protocol or BenchmarkProtocol()
    cohort = tuple(cases)
    if not cohort or any(not isinstance(case, EvaluationCase) for case in cohort):
        raise ValueError("benchmark requires a nonempty EvaluationCase cohort")
    if len({case.id for case in cohort}) != len(cohort):
        raise ValueError("benchmark case IDs must be unique")
    digest = _input_digest(cohort)
    left_warmup: list[BenchmarkCycle] = []
    right_warmup: list[BenchmarkCycle] = []
    for _ in range(plan.warmup):
        left_warmup.append(_run(baseline, cohort))
        right_warmup.append(_run(candidate, cohort))
    left: list[BenchmarkCycle] = []
    right: list[BenchmarkCycle] = []
    for repeat in range(plan.repeats):
        operations = [(baseline, left), (candidate, right)]
        if repeat % 2:
            operations.reverse()
        for engine, cycles in operations:
            cycles.append(_run(engine, cohort))
    drift = compare_cycles(left, right, plan.quality_gate)
    return BenchmarkReport(
        digest,
        cohort,
        plan,
        baseline,
        candidate,
        tuple(left),
        tuple(right),
        drift,
        tuple(left_warmup),
        tuple(right_warmup),
    )

"""UNIX entry point: JSONL on stdin/stdout; diagnostics on stderr."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys
from collections.abc import Iterator
from typing import Literal

from . import load
from .core import Request, request_from_dict
from .wire import JsonValue, decode_json


class Arguments(argparse.Namespace):
    command: Literal["decide", "evaluate", "serve", "benchmark"]
    model: str
    backend: Literal["torch", "mlx"]
    device: str | None
    max_length: int
    token_cache_size: int
    attention: str
    compile: bool
    torch_threads: int | None
    mlx_cache_limit_mib: int | None
    batch_size: int
    baseline_backend: Literal["torch", "mlx"]
    baseline_device: str | None
    baseline_batch_size: int

    port: int
    max_body_bytes: int


def _rows() -> Iterator[tuple[int, JsonValue]]:
    for number, line in enumerate(sys.stdin, 1):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            yield number, decode_json(line)
        except (ValueError, UnicodeError, RecursionError) as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"line {number}: invalid JSON") from exc


def _write(value: object) -> None:
    print(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False, separators=(",", ":")))


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run a command; explicitly requested runtime settings persist in this process."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wyat")
    subcommands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    for name in ("decide", "evaluate", "serve", "benchmark"):
        command = subcommands.add_parser(name)
        command.add_argument("model", help="local Kai artifact directory")
        command.add_argument("--backend", choices=("torch", "mlx"), default="torch")
        command.add_argument("--device", help="torch: cpu/cuda; MLX: cpu/gpu")
        command.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=2048)
        command.add_argument("--token-cache-size", type=int, default=0)
        command.add_argument("--attention", choices=("sdpa", "eager"), default="sdpa")
        command.add_argument(
            "--compile", action="store_true", help="opt-in MLX compile"
        )
        command.add_argument(
            "--torch-threads",
            type=int,
            help="process-wide PyTorch CPU threads; default leaves runtime unchanged",
        )
        command.add_argument(
            "--mlx-cache-limit-mib",
            type=int,
            help="process-wide Metal inactive-buffer cache in MiB; 0 disables caching",
        )
        if name in ("decide", "benchmark"):
            command.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=1)
        if name == "benchmark":
            command.add_argument(
                "--baseline-backend", choices=("torch", "mlx"), default="torch"
            )
            command.add_argument("--baseline-device", default="cpu")
            command.add_argument("--baseline-batch-size", type=int, default=1)
            command.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=5)
            command.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=1)
        if name == "serve":
            command.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
            command.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000)
            command.add_argument("--max-body-bytes", type=int, default=1_048_576)
    args = Arguments()
    parser.parse_args(argv, namespace=args)
    if args.command in ("decide", "benchmark") and args.batch_size <= 0:
        parser.error("--batch-size must be positive")
    if args.command == "benchmark":
        if args.baseline_batch_size <= 0 or args.repeats < 3 or args.warmup < 1:
            parser.error(
                "positive batch sizes, at least 3 repeats and 1 warmup required"
            )
    if args.torch_threads is not None and args.torch_threads <= 0:
        parser.error("--torch-threads must be positive")
    if args.mlx_cache_limit_mib is not None and not (
        0 <= args.mlx_cache_limit_mib <= sys.maxsize >> 20
    ):
        parser.error("--mlx-cache-limit-mib must fit a nonnegative byte count")
    if args.command == "serve":
        if not 1 <= args.port <= 65535:
            parser.error("--port must be between 1 and 65535")
        if args.max_body_bytes <= 0:
            parser.error("--max-body-bytes must be positive")
    try:
        if args.torch_threads is not None:
            if args.backend != "torch" and (
                args.command != "benchmark" or args.baseline_backend != "torch"
            ):
                raise ValueError("--torch-threads requires a PyTorch engine")
            import torch

            torch.set_num_threads(args.torch_threads)
        if args.mlx_cache_limit_mib is not None:
            metal_candidate = args.backend == "mlx" and args.device in (None, "gpu")
            metal_baseline = (
                args.command == "benchmark"
                and args.baseline_backend == "mlx"
                and args.baseline_device == "gpu"
            )
            if not (metal_candidate or metal_baseline):
                raise ValueError("--mlx-cache-limit-mib requires a Metal MLX engine")
            import mlx.core as mx

            if not mx.metal.is_available():
                raise ValueError("--mlx-cache-limit-mib requires available Apple Metal")
            mx.set_cache_limit(args.mlx_cache_limit_mib * (1 << 20))
        model = load(
            args.model,
            backend=args.backend,
            device=args.device,
            max_length=args.max_length,
            token_cache_size=args.token_cache_size,
            attention=args.attention,
            compile=args.compile,
        )
        if args.command == "decide":
            pending: list[Request] = []
            for number, value in _rows():
                try:
                    pending.append(request_from_dict(value))
                except ValueError as exc:
                    raise ValueError(f"line {number}: {exc}") from exc
                if len(pending) == args.batch_size:
                    for result in model.decide_many(pending):
                        _write(result.to_dict())
                    pending.clear()
            for result in model.decide_many(pending):
                _write(result.to_dict())
        elif args.command in ("evaluate", "benchmark"):
            from .evaluation import case_from_dict, evaluate

            cases = []
            for number, value in _rows():
                try:
                    cases.append(case_from_dict(value))
                except ValueError as exc:
                    raise ValueError(f"line {number}: {exc}") from exc
            if args.command == "evaluate":
                report = evaluate(model, cases)
                _write(report.to_dict())
                return 1 if report.failed else 0
            from .benchmark import BenchmarkEngine, BenchmarkProtocol, benchmark_pair

            baseline = load(
                args.model,
                backend=args.baseline_backend,
                device=args.baseline_device,
                max_length=args.max_length,
                token_cache_size=0,
            )
            benchmark = benchmark_pair(
                BenchmarkEngine(
                    "baseline",
                    baseline,
                    args.baseline_batch_size,
                    conditions={
                        "backend": args.baseline_backend,
                        "device": str(args.baseline_device),
                        "torch_threads": str(args.torch_threads),
                        "max_length": str(args.max_length),
                        "mlx_cache_limit_mib": str(args.mlx_cache_limit_mib),
                        "token_cache_size": "0",
                        "compile": "False",
                        "attention": "sdpa"
                        if args.baseline_backend == "torch"
                        else "native",
                    },
                ),
                BenchmarkEngine(
                    "candidate",
                    model,
                    args.batch_size,
                    conditions={
                        "backend": args.backend,
                        "device": args.device
                        or ("cpu" if args.backend == "torch" else "gpu"),
                        "compile": str(args.compile),
                        "token_cache_size": str(args.token_cache_size),
                        "attention": args.attention
                        if args.backend == "torch"
                        else "native",
                        "torch_threads": str(args.torch_threads),
                        "max_length": str(args.max_length),
                        "mlx_cache_limit_mib": str(args.mlx_cache_limit_mib),
                    },
                ),
                cases,
                protocol=BenchmarkProtocol(repeats=args.repeats, warmup=args.warmup),
            )
            _write(benchmark.to_dict())
            return 0 if benchmark.passed else 1
        else:
            import uvicorn

            from .server import create_app

            uvicorn.run(
                create_app(model, max_body_bytes=args.max_body_bytes),
                host=args.host,
                port=args.port,
            )
    except BrokenPipeError:
        return 0
    except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError, ImportError) as exc:
        print(f"wyat: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0

"""Select a local artifact runtime without downloading or executing model code."""

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from wyat.core import Model, Scorer


def load(
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    backend: Literal["torch", "mlx"] = "torch",
    device: str | None = None,
    max_length: int = 2048,
    token_cache_size: int = 0,
    attention: str = "sdpa",
    compile: bool = False,
) -> Model:
    """Load local Kai weights. Select the runtime explicitly; never download code.

    Torch defaults to CPU; MLX defaults to Apple GPU. Compilation is an opt-in
    MLX experiment and must pass the caller's quality and performance gates.
    """
    scorer: Scorer
    if backend == "torch":
        if compile:
            raise ValueError("compile is supported only by the MLX backend")
        from wyat.backends.kai.torch import KaiScorer

        torch_scorer = KaiScorer.from_directory(
            path,
            device="cpu" if device is None else device,
            max_length=max_length,
            token_cache_size=token_cache_size,
            attention=attention,
        )
        scorer, model_id = torch_scorer, torch_scorer.model_id
    elif backend == "mlx":
        if attention != "sdpa":
            raise ValueError("MLX uses its native attention implementation")
        from wyat.backends.kai.mlx import MLXKaiScorer

        mlx_scorer = MLXKaiScorer.from_directory(
            path,
            device="gpu" if device is None else device,
            max_length=max_length,
            token_cache_size=token_cache_size,
            compile=compile,
        )
        scorer, model_id = mlx_scorer, mlx_scorer.model_id
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported backend: {backend}")
    return Model(scorer, model_id)

"""One loaded model, one active inference, bounded HTTP request bodies."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from threading import Lock
from typing import Literal

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from fastapi import Request as HttpRequest
from starlette.concurrency import run_in_threadpool
from starlette.requests import ClientDisconnect

from .core import Model, ModelOutputError, request_from_dict
from .wire import decode_json

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def create_app(model: Model, *, max_body_bytes: int = 1_048_576) -> FastAPI:
    if isinstance(max_body_bytes, bool) or not isinstance(max_body_bytes, int):
        raise ValueError("max_body_bytes must be a positive integer")
    if max_body_bytes <= 0:
        raise ValueError("max_body_bytes must be a positive integer")
    app = FastAPI(title="Wyat", version="0.0.1")
    gate = Lock()

    @app.get("/health")
    async def health() -> dict[str, str]:
        return {"status": "ok", "model_id": model.model_id}

    @app.post("/v1/decide")
    async def decide(request: HttpRequest) -> dict[str, object]:
        data = bytearray()
        try:
            async for chunk in request.stream():
                if len(data) + len(chunk) > max_body_bytes:
                    raise HTTPException(413, "request body exceeds limit")
                data.extend(chunk)
            value = decode_json(bytes(data))
        except (ValueError, UnicodeError, RecursionError, ClientDisconnect) as exc:
            raise HTTPException(400, "invalid JSON body") from exc
        try:
            decision_request = request_from_dict(value)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise HTTPException(422, str(exc)) from exc

        if not gate.acquire(blocking=False):
            raise HTTPException(503, "model is busy; retry later")
        handoff = Lock()
        owner: Literal["queued", "running", "released"] = "queued"

        def infer() -> dict[str, object]:
            nonlocal owner
            with handoff:
                if owner != "queued":
                    raise HTTPException(503, "inference admission was withdrawn")
                owner = "running"
            try:
                return model.decide(decision_request).to_dict()
            finally:
                # A cancelled handler cannot release a running worker's slot.
                with handoff:
                    owner = "released"
                    gate.release()

        try:
            # Blocking inference runs off the event loop. The gate also protects
            # the scorer's tokenizer and tensor state across HTTP requests.
            return await run_in_threadpool(infer)
        except HTTPException:
            raise
        except ModelOutputError as exc:
            logger.exception("model output contract failed")
            raise HTTPException(500, "model inference failed") from exc
        except ValueError as exc:
            # Backend input-policy errors must not echo submitted prompt text.
            raise HTTPException(422, "request is unsupported by this model") from exc
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.exception("model inference failed")
            raise HTTPException(500, "model inference failed") from exc
        finally:
            # Cancellation or dispatch failure may happen before a worker starts.
            # Withdraw atomically so a late callback cannot enter inference.
            with handoff:
                if owner == "queued":
                    owner = "released"
                    gate.release()

    return app

"""One owned current-CLI comparison; no framework imports in the supervisor."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import hashlib
import json
import os
import platform
import signal
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

ROOT = Path("/Users/teilomillet/Code/wyat")
MODEL = ROOT / ".models/Decision-2.0-Kai-0.6B"
OUTPUT = ROOT / "benchmarks/real/runtime-cpu-mlx77-current.json"
DECLARATION = Path("/private/tmp/wyat-cpu-prefix-production-audit.py")
DECLARATION_SHA = "2353659ee2a2a1960581d90fa9bc1e33574a5d520a166e74f3cb838303f28a0b"


def digest(path: Path) -> str:
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        return hashlib.file_digest(handle, "sha256").hexdigest()


def constants() -> dict[str, object]:
    if digest(DECLARATION) != DECLARATION_SHA:
        raise ValueError("Immutable asset declaration changed")
    values: dict[str, object] = {}
    for node in ast.parse(DECLARATION.read_text()).body:
        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
            for target in node.targets:
                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id in (
                    "MODEL_FILES",
                    "DATA_SHA",
                    "REFERENCE_SHA",
                    "MODEL_ID",
                    "INPUT_SHA",
                ):
                    values[target.id] = ast.literal_eval(node.value)
    return values


def main() -> int:
    if any(OUTPUT.parent.glob(OUTPUT.stem + ".*")):
        raise FileExistsError("Preserve existing receipts")
    declared = constants()
    dataset = ROOT / "benchmarks/real/banking77-train-dev-menu6.jsonl"
    reference = ROOT / "benchmarks/real/torch-fp32-reference77.json"
    assets = {
        MODEL / name: checksum
        for name, checksum in cast(dict[str, str], declared["MODEL_FILES"]).items()
    }
    assets.update(
        {
            dataset: cast(str, declared["DATA_SHA"]),
            reference: cast(str, declared["REFERENCE_SHA"]),
        }
    )
    if any(digest(path) != checksum for path, checksum in assets.items()):
        raise ValueError("Pinned assets differ")
    sources = sorted((ROOT / "wyat").rglob("*.py")) + [Path(__file__)]
    installed = ROOT / ".venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages"
    for name in (
        "mlx_lm/models/qwen3.py",
        "mlx_lm/models/qwen2.py",
        "mlx_lm/models/base.py",
        "transformers/models/qwen3/modeling_qwen3.py",
        "transformers/integrations/sdpa_attention.py",
    ):
        sources.append(installed / name)
    rows = [
        {"path": str(path), "sha256": digest(path), "text": path.read_text()}
        for path in sources
    ]
    archive = OUTPUT.with_suffix(".sources.json")
    archive.write_text(json.dumps({"files": rows}, indent=2) + "\n")
    command = [
        str(ROOT / ".venv/bin/python"),
        "-m",
        "wyat",
        "benchmark",
        str(MODEL),
        "--backend",
        "mlx",
        "--device",
        "gpu",
        "--baseline-backend",
        "torch",
        "--baseline-device",
        "cpu",
        "--batch-size",
        "1",
        "--baseline-batch-size",
        "1",
        "--max-length",
        "512",
        "--token-cache-size",
        "0",
        "--torch-threads",
        "8",
        "--repeats",
        "5",
        "--warmup",
        "1",
        "--mlx-cache-limit-mib",
        "512",
    ]
    wall: dict[str, object] = {
        "command": command,
        "stdin": str(dataset),
        "timeout_seconds": 180,
        "completed": False,
        "timed_out": False,
        "exit_code": None,
        "source_archive": {"path": str(archive), "sha256": digest(archive)},
        "asset_sha256": {str(path): checksum for path, checksum in assets.items()},
        "model_id": declared["MODEL_ID"],
        "input_sha256": declared["INPUT_SHA"],
        "host": platform.platform(),
        "environment": {"MLX_ENABLE_TF32": "0"},
        "limits": [
            "Same logical requests; physical padding differs between backends",
            "CLI exit is quality status, not the four performance gates",
            "Timeout has unknown partial outcomes; no progress journal",
            "Shared cumulative RSS is not per-arm memory",
        ],
    }
    wall_path = OUTPUT.with_suffix(".wall.json")

    def save() -> None:
        wall_path.write_text(json.dumps(wall, indent=2, allow_nan=False) + "\n")

    save()
    started = time.perf_counter()
    with (
        dataset.open("rb") as stdin,
        OUTPUT.open("x") as stdout,
        OUTPUT.with_suffix(".log").open("x") as stderr,
    ):
        child = subprocess.Popen(
            command,
            cwd=ROOT,
            stdin=stdin,
            stdout=stdout,
            stderr=stderr,
            start_new_session=True,
            env={**os.environ, "MLX_ENABLE_TF32": "0"},
        )
        try:
            wall["pid"] = child.pid
            save()
            code = child.wait(timeout=180)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            wall["timed_out"] = True
            code = 124
        finally:
            try:
                os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass
            child.wait()
            wall["reaped"] = True
    wall.update(
        exit_code=code,
        completed=code == 0,
        elapsed_seconds=time.perf_counter() - started,
        source_verified_after=all(
            digest(Path(row["path"])) == row["sha256"] for row in rows
        ),
        asset_verified_after=all(
            digest(path) == checksum for path, checksum in assets.items()
        ),
        stdout_sha256=digest(OUTPUT),
        log_sha256=digest(OUTPUT.with_suffix(".log")),
    )
    verified = (
        wall["source_verified_after"] is True and wall["asset_verified_after"] is True
    )
    wall["evidence_verified"] = verified
    save()
    print(json.dumps(wall, allow_nan=False))
    return code if verified else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Decisions needed for production Wyat inference

These questions do not block the local Kai reference backend or the generic
logit-scorer API. They block selecting and validating the eventual Wyat model
contract and claiming a production performance or quality target.

1. **Which checkpoint and export contract will be promoted from training?**
   Kayak's released CLM, its joint models, and CLM Lab's validity model differ.
   The export must name the family/version, rendering and segmented tokenization,
   pooling, head shape, candidate limits, score interpretation/calibration,
   adapter base revision, and hashes. See `docs/training-contracts.md`.
2. **Which deployment hardware and request distribution define “20× vanilla”?**
   Freeze the device, runtime, precision, CPU threads, contexts, candidate counts,
   batch sizes/concurrency, repeated-candidate rate, warm/cold conditions, baseline
   implementation, and p50/p95/p99 or throughput objective. A tokenization-only
   improvement does not establish a full-engine speedup.
3. **What labeled development and reserved confirmation cohort gates quality?**
   Specify accepted metrics and tolerances for logits, ranking disagreements,
   task accuracy, abstention, and calibration. Real Kai CPU/MLX parity is now
   measured on a frozen BANKING77 training-source development assay. Prior model
   exposure is unknown, so it cannot gate held-out Wyat model quality. DMBench
   owns benchmark definitions and provenance; Wyat supplies inference adapters.
4. **Which externally exposed deployment boundary is authorized?**
   The supplied server runs locally. Production hosting, authentication/TLS,
   resource budgets, and model access should follow the chosen deployment.
No answer has been invented for these choices. Work can continue mechanically
on the reference backend and its evidence while training contracts develop.

"""Stock tiny Qwen3 oracles; synthetic mechanics do not establish learned quality."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

import pytest
import torch
from hypothesis import HealthCheck, given, settings
from hypothesis import strategies as st
from torch import nn
from transformers import Qwen3Config, Qwen3Model
from transformers.cache_utils import DynamicCache, DynamicLayer
from transformers.integrations import sdpa_attention
from transformers.masking_utils import create_causal_mask
from transformers.modeling_outputs import BaseModelOutputWithPast
from transformers.models.qwen3.modeling_qwen3 import (
    Qwen3Attention,
    Qwen3DecoderLayer,
    Qwen3RMSNorm,
)

from benchmarks.analysis.torch.readout import block as experiment


def tiny() -> Qwen3Model:
    config = Qwen3Config(
        vocab_size=32,
        hidden_size=16,
        intermediate_size=32,
        num_hidden_layers=2,
        num_attention_heads=4,
        num_key_value_heads=2,
        head_dim=8,
        max_position_embeddings=64,
        attention_dropout=0.0,
        rope_parameters={"rope_type": "default", "rope_theta": 10000.0},
    )
    config._attn_implementation = "sdpa"
    with torch.random.fork_rng():
        torch.manual_seed(21)
        model = Qwen3Model(config)
        cast(nn.Module, model).eval()
        return model


def seed(
    model: Qwen3Model, length: int
) -> tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], ...]:
    with torch.inference_mode():
        output = cast(
            BaseModelOutputWithPast,
            model(
                input_ids=torch.arange(length)[None] % 32,
                use_cache=True,
            ),
        )
        assert type(output.past_key_values) is DynamicCache
        return tuple(
            (layer.keys.clone(), layer.values.clone())
            for layer in output.past_key_values.layers
            if isinstance(layer, DynamicLayer)
            and layer.keys is not None
            and layer.values is not None
        )


def fork(
    model: Qwen3Model,
    states: tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], ...],
    batch: int,
) -> DynamicCache:
    with torch.inference_mode():
        return DynamicCache(
            config=model.config,
            ddp_cache_data=tuple(
                (k.expand(batch, -1, -1, -1), v.expand(batch, -1, -1, -1))
                for k, v in states
            ),
        )


def prepare(
    model: Qwen3Model,
    suffix: torch.Tensor,
    cache: DynamicCache,
    prefix: int,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor]:
    """Maintained lower blocks/mask/RoPE before the final-layer experiment."""
    with torch.inference_mode():
        hidden = model.embed_tokens(suffix)
        positions = torch.arange(prefix, prefix + suffix.shape[1])[None]
        embeddings = cast(
            tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], model.rotary_emb(hidden, positions)
        )
        mask = create_causal_mask(
            config=model.config,
            inputs_embeds=hidden,
            attention_mask=None,
            past_key_values=cache,
            position_ids=positions,
        )
        assert isinstance(mask, torch.Tensor)
        for layer in model.layers[:-1]:
            hidden = layer(
                hidden,
                attention_mask=mask,
                position_embeddings=embeddings,
                position_ids=positions,
                past_key_values=cache,
                use_cache=True,
            )
        return hidden, embeddings, mask


def evaluate(
    model: Qwen3Model,
    states: tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], ...],
    suffix: torch.Tensor,
    positions: torch.Tensor,
    prefix: int,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, DynamicCache]:
    cache = fork(model, states, suffix.shape[0])
    hidden, embeddings, _ = prepare(model, suffix, cache, prefix)
    assert cache.get_seq_length(0) == prefix + suffix.shape[1]
    assert cache.get_seq_length(1) == prefix
    result = experiment.selected_last_block(
        cast(Qwen3DecoderLayer, model.layers[-1]),
        model.norm,
        hidden,
        positions,
        embeddings,
        cache,
        prefix_length=prefix,
    )
    return result, cache


@settings(
    max_examples=12,
    deadline=None,
    derandomize=True,
    suppress_health_check=[HealthCheck.function_scoped_fixture],
)
@given(prefix=st.integers(1, 5), length=st.integers(2, 12), batch=st.integers(1, 3))
def test_stock_full_hidden_oracle_ragged_duplicates_and_absolute_rope(
    tmp_path: Path,
    prefix: int,
    length: int,
    batch: int,
) -> None:
    model = tiny()
    states = seed(model, prefix)
    suffix = (torch.arange(batch * length).reshape(batch, length) + 7) % 32
    selected = torch.tensor(
        [
            [0, max(0, length - row - 2), max(0, length - row - 2), 0]
            for row in range(batch)
        ]
    )
    # Row-dependent right padding follows every real readout, including query overlap.
    for row in range(batch):
        suffix[row, max(1, length - row) :] = 0
    actual, cache = evaluate(model, states, suffix, selected, prefix)
    full_ids = torch.cat(
        (torch.arange(prefix)[None].expand(batch, -1) % 32, suffix), dim=1
    )
    with torch.inference_mode():
        full = model(input_ids=full_ids, use_cache=False).last_hidden_state
        expected = full[torch.arange(batch)[:, None], prefix + selected]
    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5)
    assert cache.get_seq_length(1) == prefix + length
    assert torch.equal(actual[:, 1], actual[:, 2])
    assert torch.equal(actual[:, 0], actual[:, 3])
    changed = suffix.clone()
    changed[:, -1] = (changed[:, -1] + 1) % 32
    causal, _ = evaluate(model, states, changed, selected, prefix)
    torch.testing.assert_close(causal, actual, atol=0, rtol=0)
    evidence = {
        "prefix": prefix,
        "suffix_length": length,
        "batch": batch,
        "positions": selected.tolist(),
        "expected": expected.tolist(),
        "actual": actual.tolist(),
        "future_perturbed": causal.tolist(),
        "max_abs_difference": (actual - expected).abs().max().item(),
    }
    (tmp_path / f"p{prefix}-s{length}-b{batch}.json").write_text(json.dumps(evidence))


def test_full_stock_final_block_and_batch_specific_rope_oracle() -> None:
    model = tiny()
    states = seed(model, 3)

    positions = torch.tensor([[3, 0, 3], [1, 2, 1]])

    hidden, embeddings, mask = prepare(model, suffix, control, 3)
    embeddings = (
        embeddings[0].expand(2, -1, -1).contiguous(),
        embeddings[1].expand(2, -1, -1).contiguous(),
    )
    with torch.inference_mode():
        expected = model.norm(
            model.layers[-1](
                hidden,
                attention_mask=mask,
                position_embeddings=embeddings,

            embeddings,

    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5)


def test_snapshot_interleaving_consumed_owner_and_failure_recovery(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
) -> None:
    model = tiny()
    states = seed(model, 2)
    copies = tuple((k.clone(), v.clone()) for k, v in states)
    suffix = torch.tensor([[4, 5, 6]])
    positions = torch.tensor([[0, 2, 0]])
    before, cache = evaluate(model, states, suffix, positions, 2)
    evaluate(model, states, torch.tensor([[9, 8], [5, 4]]), torch.tensor([[0], [1]]), 2)
    after, _ = evaluate(model, states, suffix, positions, 2)
    torch.testing.assert_close(after, before, atol=0, rtol=0)
    hidden, embeddings, _ = prepare(model, suffix, fork(model, states, 1), 2)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="fresh"):
        experiment.selected_last_block(
            cast(Qwen3DecoderLayer, model.layers[-1]),
            model.norm,
            hidden,
            positions,
            embeddings,
            cache,
            prefix_length=2,
        )
    failed_cache = fork(model, states, 1)
    original = experiment.sdpa_attention_forward

    def fail(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None]:
        raise RuntimeError("suffix failure after append")

    monkeypatch.setattr(experiment, "sdpa_attention_forward", fail)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="suffix failure"):
        experiment.selected_last_block(
            cast(Qwen3DecoderLayer, model.layers[-1]),
            model.norm,
            hidden,
            positions,
            embeddings,
            failed_cache,
            prefix_length=2,
        )
    assert failed_cache.get_seq_length(1) == 5
    monkeypatch.setattr(experiment, "sdpa_attention_forward", original)
    recovered, _ = evaluate(model, states, suffix, positions, 2)
    torch.testing.assert_close(recovered, before, atol=0, rtol=0)
    assert all(
        torch.equal(a, b)
        for pair, saved in zip(states, copies, strict=True)
        for a, b in zip(pair, saved, strict=True)
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

        "autocast",

def test_unsupported_before_projection_or_cache_mutation(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,

) -> None:
    model = tiny()
    states = seed(model, 2)
    cache = fork(model, states, 1)
    hidden, embeddings, _ = prepare(model, torch.tensor([[4, 5, 6]]), cache, 2)
    positions = torch.tensor([[0, 2]])
    if kind == "autocast":
        monkeypatch.setattr(torch, "is_autocast_enabled", lambda device: True)
    elif kind == "training":
        model.layers[-1].train()
    elif kind == "hook":
        model.layers[-1].register_forward_hook(lambda *args: None)
    elif kind == "dtype":
        hidden = hidden.double()
    elif kind == "rope":
        model.config.rope_parameters = {"rope_type": "dynamic", "rope_theta": 10000.0}
    elif kind == "index":
        positions[0, 1] = 3
    elif kind == "cache":

        class Foreign(DynamicCache):
            pass

        cache = Foreign(config=model.config)

    norm = model.norm
    if kind == "embeddings":
        embeddings = cast(tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor], (embeddings[0],))
    elif kind == "norm":
        norm = Qwen3RMSNorm(8).eval()
    elif kind == "gradient":
        hidden = hidden.clone().requires_grad_()
    elif kind == "index_dtype":
        positions = positions.int()

    def forbidden(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> torch.Tensor:

    monkeypatch.setattr(

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        experiment.selected_last_block(

@pytest.mark.skipif(
    not (
